ST_VisionArchives.PaperCastle_RecordBefore_1:
"…Uh, do I have to fill this part out too? Alright then…
So here's what happened. I'm an artist, and I usually dabble in street art. But lately, the Bopp been causing quite a ruckus. They've taken over all the graffiti walls I usually go to! You know how it is, the Bopp aren't as reasonable as human artists. They're really aggressive! Anyone who dares to paint over their masterpieces is gonna get beaten up! I'm getting off track here… Anyway, I really had nowhere to express my creativity, so I had a bright idea to find some manholes on the street to beautify. Wouldn't get in anyone's way, wouldn't mess up the city's appearance, and the Security Office probably wouldn't mind… right?
I thought I was a genius, so I grabbed my paint and went looking for manholes. But as soon as I got to the street, I saw something round and golden in the distance that looked like a patterned manhole cover. I thought maybe a fellow artist had the same idea, so I got closer to take a better look… Suddenly, fog started rising all around… when it cleared, the sky had turned a sickly yellow color. There were trees and streetlights made of cardboard everywhere… and this castle that looked like a stage prop from a play.
Even then, I still thought it was some installation art by that fellow artist, so I wasn't scared at all. While I was trying to figure it out, that castle sprung to life! First it shot out some streamers, then it set up a bunch of machine guns and cannons and started firing at me. I got so scared I couldn't think about anything else and just ran… I ran really far, and when I looked back, everything was gone. When I looked up at the sky, it was blue again, like it was all just a dream.
I'm not saying I miss it or anything! Thank goodness that creepy thing didn't chase after me… Though, I have to admit, that pop-up book design was actually pretty creative and really sparked my imagination… I'm just saying, next time, I'm definitely going to stick to finding empty walls for graffiti. No more bright ideas!"
ST_VisionArchives.BuildingDrawing_Record_2:
"Interview me? Heh heh… I didn't realize The Coluccis' reputation had spread so far already! Huh? T-that's not what this is about?
Oh… you mean that building? I did wander over there last week and ran into this annoying Anomaly… Right! The one you mentioned, that pile of messy papers!
I'd just finished some super crispy mackerel at Noetic Bridge and wanted to find a building for some 360 parkour! Perfect for digesting while enjoying the scenery! So I set my sights on that construction site… Hey, don't worry about how I got in…! Anyway, I just wandered around the building for a bit, and when I reached the rooftop that's when I bumped into that Anomaly.
At first, I thought it was something like a Chatterflyer, so I wanted to see what was written on the paper. Before I could get a good look, it suddenly lunged at me and pulled me into the Anomalous Realm! Hmph! No manners at all!
What was it like inside? Just a similar building… Oh! I remember now, doing parkour in that building inside the Anomalous Realm was way more interesting than outside! Its exterior walls had all sorts of weird stuff on them, like obstacles set up just for me! As the Ichi-daime of The Coluccis, how could I refuse a challenge after receiving such an invitation!
Uh… well, I did run into a little trouble… I finally managed to climb to the rooftop, but apparently that didn't count! I had to collect all the blueprints that thing had scattered around. But when I got them, I couldn't understand what was drawn on them at all. They did chatter on about something, but I couldn't make heads or tails of it…
A-anyway! I eventually got sent out of that Anomalous Realm! Which proves I completed the challenge… Right! That's exactly what happened!"
ST_VisionArchives.ColorsMerge_RecordBefore_2:
"Turns out these Inspiration Terminators don't just swipe a single idea. They go after the whole network of connected thoughts.
I learned this the hard way, and honestly? It's mortifying. Here's how it went down:
I'd just sent my latest manuscript to my editor and was finally ready to breathe, but my brain wouldn't quit. Figuring I should use the momentum, I started sketching out spinoff ideas… and that's when it hit me.
One second, my thoughts were flowing fast and clear. The next? It felt like slamming into a brick wall. Total mental gridlock! The worst part? It wasn't just the spinoffs that vanished… When my editor called to discuss revisions, my mind went completely blank on my own book! I just stammered like an idiot, and all I could think was, "Why did I write it that way? What was I even thinking?"
The fog didn't lift until I got an Anomaly Hunter to deal with the Terminator. Suddenly, the stack of blank pages on my desk was my manuscript again. Looking back, it makes sense. Those spinoffs were tangled up with the world and themes of the main story. The Terminator didn't just steal the idea I was working on; it blocked everything tied to it.
Yeah, you can bet I'm stocking up on industrial-strength bug spray before my next writing session."
ST_VisionArchives.SchoolMyth_RecordBefore_3:
"First bell rings.
When I rushed into the school building this morning with bread in my mouth, I absolutely never imagined I'd be performing slapstick comedy in the hallway. I face-planted on flat ground, and when I grimaced and crawled back up, the bread in my mouth had already been smashed into a desperate mask of pain when I used my face to soften my fall…
Fifth bell rings.
I'm out of time! When I rushed to the second floor corner, something even weirder happened. My backpack strap was suddenly yanked by some mysterious force, making me feel like a puppet pinned in place. An invisible force was blocking my progress! Though when I turned around, all I could see was the fire extinguisher door swaying slightly. The classroom was clearly right in front of me, yet I felt like I couldn't move an inch—like that powerless feeling when you're running in a dream, where a one-meter distance stretches into an endless abyss of helplessness…
Eighth bell rings.
Haha, I'm already about to be late anyway, might as well take my time… The hall monitor at the end of the corridor is already writing down my name. He adjusted his glasses and asked why I wouldn't enter the classroom, why I was standing in the middle of the hallway confronting him. Dude… it's not that I don't want to walk, I feel like there's a massive weight on my feet. It's not super glue stuck to them! It's not a leg cramp either! I swear there's some invisible guy pulling on me. The hall monitor adjusted his glasses again, saying he'd heard this kind of excuse plenty of times, and he stopped believing me from the first word I said.
Ninth bell rings.
The hall monitor walks toward me…
Tenth bell rings.
The hall monitor rolls toward me…
Twelfth bell rings.
Someone save me and the hall monitor—we've been bounced around the hallway like two rubber balls by some invisible force!!
Thirteenth bell rings.
Thankfully, I finally made it into the classroom. Though not through the front door… I crashed through the wall.
Hey, hall monitor, don't worry about whether anything's broken. Your right hand still works, right? Cross my name off that list! I got in before the thirteenth bell, so it doesn't count as being late, right?"
ST_VisionArchives.ZhangYuChe_RecordBefore_3:
From a battle perspective, this thing isn't too tough. You just need to watch out for its frontal charge while keeping an eye on sneak attacks from its tentacles. The high danger rating is mostly based on its destructive power, and honestly, its destructive power lives up to that rating. It's fine when it's not in battle mode, but once it enters battle mode, everything standing nearby is probably going to get smashed.
By the way, you should still be careful when fighting it. After all, nobody can tell if its tentacles retreating into the truck means it's scared or if it's been hit with Nullification. What if you let your guard down and it suddenly sticks out a tentacle to grab you and lift you up? These are all lessons learned from others' blood and tears… I'm getting off track. So, it's best to consider the octopus part separating from the truck as the signal of victory. That's the safest choice.
That's all for my experience sharing. Hope it helps any Anomaly Hunters looking to deal with this Anomaly. Ahem, I'll stay anonymous this time…
ST_VisionArchives.ZhangYuChe_VisionDescAfter:
An oddity with decent camouflage abilities that occasionally appears on roads throughout Hethereau in the form of an old trailer truck with octopus tentacles. Under normal circumstances, Octowpus will try its best to follow traffic rules to blend into its surroundings, but there are also cases where Octowpus attacks nearby pedestrians and facilities. Since it's impossible to predict when it will attack, citizens are advised to keep their distance once they spot Octowpus. For Anomaly Hunters, Octowpus is highly sensitive to threats in its vicinity. Once you enter its alert range, it will immediately drop its disguise and prepare for battle, destroying the surrounding environment and blocking traffic to create a favorable battle zone for itself.
Until Octowpus is nullified or leaves on its own, any moving object that enters the battle area will be considered an enemy and attacked. Therefore, blocked traffic can only be restored after Octowpus disappears.
ST_VisionArchives.SchoolMyth_CusConmment_2_Dis_Player:
They're truly afraid of being alone.
Clumsily designing games, carefully adjusting the difficulty, all just to make participants stay a little longer. They desperately hope that those who leave might return due to various coincidences—whether it's forgotten keys, sudden downpours, or simply thinking the game wasn't half bad…
"Want to play another round?" When they see returning participants, they'll quietly ask with heads down, though inside they're already bursting with joy.
ST_VisionArchives.SchoolMyth_VisionDescAfter:
Regarding the strange behaviors exhibited by the Wandering Puppets, all witnesses describe a sense of "being deliberately guided to participate in games." This may suggest they possess a need for companionship.
When participants actively propose "performance invitations" to the dolls, all abnormal activities immediately cease and transform into courteous interactions. The musical doll will voluntarily give up the piano bench and turn pages for the participant during their performance; beneath the baking doll's cup lies delicious sweets carefully prepared for the participant; the running doll prefers to jog shoulder-to-shoulder with participants rather than compete for speed, aimlessly circling the playground together while enjoying the evening breeze.
Once the dolls sense kind responses from participants, their loneliness dissipates. They'll then return to the art room on their own, remaining inactive for the following week.
It is recommended to maintain monthly "Social Gatherings" as this is currently the most effective containment measure. They never wanted to win the games—they just wanted friends.
ST_VisionArchives.PaperCastle_RecordBefore_3:
Bureau of Anomaly Control Internal Document

Clearance: Internal Public
Department: Containment Unit 2
Submitted by: Mint

Review Report on Failed Containment of Expired Invitation

An incident occurred during today's containment of Anomaly C-1704 Expired Invitation, and it's all Mint's fault… After receiving a citizen's distress call, Mint's team immediately arrived on scene and entered the Expired Invitation's Anomalous Realm. We prioritized ensuring the safety of the trapped citizen, then prepared to contain the Anomaly according to protocol. Following the New Containment Safety Protocol, we had prepared the containment vessel in advance, but while weakening the Anomaly, Mint saw those two paper streamers swaying back and forth, and suddenly felt this irresistible urge and lunged at them… By the time Mint came to her senses, those two streamers were already torn down, and the Anomaly was directly nullified… We had no choice but to bring back the treasure chest it left behind to the Bureau. It's currently placed in Temporary Containment, scheduled to be processed separately as an anomalous derivative later. Looking back, it's still really strange. Why did that happen? Could this Anomaly also have had mental control abilities? Mint definitely wasn't asleep when reviewing the materials…

Anyway! Mint feels deeply guilty about this mistake and formally apologize to the other team members. Mint is sorry! My teammates operated completely according to protocol during this containment operation. Mint requests that only my salary be docked! T T

Team Member Opinion 1: The salary is a minor issue, but next time let's not assign Mint to containment quests for Anomalies with… colorful dangling objects.
Team Member Opinion 2: Also try not to assign her to quests with yarn balls…
ST_VisionArchives.PaperCastle_RecordBefore_2:
"I'm not here asking you to deal with Anomalies. I'm an Anomaly Hunter myself! Don't let my current appearance fool you, I've got several rookies under me… Sure, they're pretty green, but for this level of Anomaly, why would I need to ask the Bureau for help?
You've heard of the Expired Invitation Anomaly, right? I first encountered it about four or five years ago. I was new to the business back then, and my luck wasn't great. I'd gone several days without any work. My account was nearly empty, and I was about to go hungry when I saw Hyelp post a new commission. I didn't even think twice before accepting it. When I got to the quest location, I realized this thing was incredibly tough to deal with. My skill level back then wasn't nearly enough to handle it. After getting beaten and having to flee embarrassingly several times, it actually sparked my competitive spirit. Luckily, this commission had no time limit, so every day I'd take down a few small fry to earn meal money, then spend the rest of my time studying the Expired Invitation. After messing around with it for over half a month, I finally discovered the true purpose of the Expired Invitation.
Think about it: touch it and you enter the Anomalous Realm, enter the Realm and you get swarmed. Escaping isn't that hard though, so there's no real risk. After you escape, it turns back into a wax seal… but the next time you go there, it triggers again. Isn't that just an indestructible, self-repairing target dummy? Perfect for practice! Once I figured this out, I managed to convince the original client to let me keep it and rent it out to rookie Anomaly Hunters as a training tool. Business was booming! The Fons it earned me far exceeded the original commission fee. Every day, rookies would come to rent this 'Expired Invitation' from me. Sure, they'd always tease me saying 'If there really are demons in this world, every demon would have your tattoo on them'… but I was really broke! Wanting to make money isn't shameful!
…So, my request? Uh, didn't I already say? I don't want to nullify the Anomaly. I just want to ask around and see if you know where there might be other Expired Invitations. A couple days ago, some rookie accidentally nullified the one I was renting out… Now everyone can't use such a versitile and cheap practice tool. So I… Hey, I wasn't finished talking yet!"

ST_VisionArchives.ColorsMerge_RecordBefore_3:
"It's not exactly a troublesome Anomaly. Usually you just rush in and clean house. But even so, every time we get this kind of commission, everyone in our team becomes extremely polite and courteous. They decline and defer to each other until we have to draw lots to see which poor soul gets to 'hit the jackpot.'
You know how Inspiration Terminators create Anomalous Realms based on exaggerated versions of the inspiration they absorb, right? Basically, it becomes a massive theme park of materialized ideas. Just by standing there, you know exactly what the person whose idea got stolen was thinking.
This is… definitely not fun. Let me put it this way: I once got a commission from the manga artist I admire. If I didn't help solve her big problem, the ending of her series would be… Anyway, with the devout and anxious feeling of being able to help my idol, I stepped into the Anomalous Realm, only to discover it was generated from her inspiration for the final chapter! Completely caught off guard, I got thoroughly spoiled… All the anticipation from following the series, the excitement of discussing plot threads with others, all the satisfaction that belonged to this work… it was all shattered so carelessly and hastily. I should have… I should have celebrated with my friends as it reached its final chapter, reading through this story slowly with both happiness and reluctance…
Ahem, I'm getting off track. Anyway, these Anomalous Realms generated from people's inspiration are even more complex than those created by other Anomalies. If the inspiration owner is a horror film director, congratulations on earning an unforgettably terrifying experience. A colleague of mine almost got lost in a mystery novelist's inspiration space, which really gave everyone quite a scare. Does PTSD count as a work injury?
Oh, and here's the most important point. Usually we're required to sign confidentiality agreements and whatnot. After all, we're the only ones besides the client who know about these ideas. While I can understand it, all those rules and regulations are just so annoying! The commission fee isn't that high, but there's no shortage of restrictions! It's no wonder nobody wants to take these jobs…"
ST_VisionArchives.SchoolMyth_VisionDescBefore:
This Anomaly appears as standard artist mannequins commonly found in art classrooms, with articulated joints that allow them to mimic human limb movements. Their current numbers remain unknown. The dolls lack any sense of privacy or shame and show no interest in wearing clothing. Since they only appear during nighttime (20:00–06:00), they effectively avoid violating the school's dress code policies.
Early on, the Wandering Puppets attempted daytime activities, including substituting for a student suffering from Delayed Sleep Phase Syndrome (a condition common among teenagers and night owls). When the teacher called the student's name during attendance, the doll's inability to produce normal vocal sounds led to the teacher publicly criticizing it with "Are you made of wood?" This comment proved prophetic, causing the teacher to suffer a heart condition from excessive shock. The substitute doll was subsequently dismantled and permanently stored in the storage room.
Currently, dolls with detectable activity within the school grounds include Welcome-type, Sprint-type, Shell Game-type, Performance-type, and Hide-and-Seek-type variants. All exhibit strong social needs and actively initiate "games" to gain companionship and interaction from human targets. When the dolls sense declining attention, they may develop punitive attitudes toward their game partners. It is recommended to respect the dolls' game rules—refusing to play equals voluntary surrender. They never punish rule-breakers… but the games will continue forever.
ST_VisionArchives.ColorsMerge_VisionDescAfter:
"This Bio Anomaly resembles flies and other insects in appearance. It typically attaches to the victim's head and absorbs inspiration through its mouthparts. After obtaining a considerable amount of inspiration, it constructs an Anomalous Realm to hide in. Nullifying an Inspiration Terminator requires entering the Anomalous Realm and reaching its hideout. Since the Anomalous Realm is composed of inspiration consumed by the Terminator, its content is often complex, variable, and irregular. Anomaly Hunters must adapt on the fly and respond flexibly.
After reclaiming the stolen inspiration, the Anomalous Realm will change accordingly. It should be noted that the rules within Anomalous Realms often follow specific logic. Understanding these rules will be very helpful for nullification work."
ST_VisionArchives.ColorsMerge_RecordBefore_1:
"Everyone says Inspiration Terminators are creators' mortal enemies. Wherever they show up, it's like a swarm of locusts passing through, not a single good idea is left behind. But I need to set the record straight about these annoying little pests: they're picky eaters.
That's right, I actually saw one feeding. It wobbled down, fluttering weakly before crash-landing on its victim's head. You could tell it hadn't eaten in ages, it was so hungry it could barely stay airborne.
Unfortunately, the guy's thick hair blocked my view, so I couldn't see just how it sucked out the inspiration. All I could make out from a distance was a tiny dot starting to glow in that mess of hair. I figured it had done its thing, I grabbed my fly swatter, held my breath, and waited…
But then? That glowing dot floated back up, flickering erratically. Suddenly, it convulsed and spat out a dull, grayish orb of light. The orb drifted right back to its owner, while the Inspiration Terminator just hung there, dazed. Seizing my chance, I swatted the Terminator out of the air.
The guy at the desk had no clue what happened. He just stayed hunched over, scribbling away like mad. Makes you wonder… what kind of "inspiration" did he get back? Clearly, the Terminator found it so disgusting it'd rather starve than keep it down."
ST_VisionArchives.Sadbear_RecordBefore_3:
#MyChildhoodFriends
Thanks for the invitation. When I came across this topic, I happened to be cleaning up at home and stumbled upon my childhood diary, one of those expensive password journals from the corner store back then. I couldn't remember the password anymore, but since so much time had passed, the plastic casing of the lock had become very brittle and I pried it open easily. Even though I was 100% sure it was my own diary, the unfamiliar handwriting and events I had no memory of made it feel like I was peeking into someone else's diary.
Maybe I'm setting this up too much, but anyway… I found some pretty interesting stuff, so I wanted to record it on Bagel.
"Why can't Mommy and Daddy see Nini? Nini is sitting right there on the bench, her white dress is so pretty, I want a dress just like hers too, but Mommy won't buy it for me."
"Amai said he couldn't see Nini either, so I told him Nini has two braids and wears a really pretty white dress, and she's as tall as me, then Amai could see Nini too. I also told Linlin and Songzi, and they could all see Nini. Only the grown-ups can't see her, oh well, I guess grown-ups don't know everything after all."
"Linlin said his friend is really strong, and it's true, he can lift a chair with one hand. Amai's friend is a bit shy, but he's willing to play with us too. Songzi's friend is a white little dog, and we all got to pet it. This is our secret."
"Nini is a bad person, I hate her."
"Nini gave me her little bear toy, and we made up."
…
"Linlin can't see Nini anymore, I told him Nini is right next to me, and he said I was lying, he doesn't want to play with me anymore. But Amai and Songzi can still see her, so I don't want to play with Linlin anymore either."
…
"Amai's friend disappeared, and Songzi's little dog is gone too. I asked Songzi where his white little dog was, and Songzi said he never had any white little dog, all their friends are gone."
"Now only I can see Nini."
…
"Why can't they all see her? They all say I'm lying, that I'm making it all up… But I'm not lying, Nini is right here."
"Amai doesn't want to play with me anymore either, so I lied, I said I couldn't see Nini anymore too. Then I could play with Amai and the others again, but I still like playing with Nini the most."
…
After that, "Nini" never appeared again. I messaged my parents to ask, and they said I never had a friend named Nini when I was little. They did buy me a few teddy bears though, but they don't know where those went either. Kids really are so imaginative.
The rest of the diary wasn't very interesting, so I'm planning to organize all this stuff and throw it out as recyclables. No follow-up.
ST_VisionArchives.Boss08_Record_1:
Recording

I saw Swallowtail on my way to the cinema. A large butterfly of vibrant colors, wanting to soar high but weighed down by the paper scraps on its body, left dreaming of escaping the world. It had no idea that even if it really flew up into the sky, it would still be tied down to this world. There's no escape. No one can escape.
3 seconds of silence
She was terrified of fire. She was afraid those ticket stubs would burn. She loved watching movies. She felt that compared to real life, movies were more worthwhile. Everything dormant would be stirred awake, everything unresolved would be promised an ending. Unlike real life, which is always a chaotic mess… In life, she was a fly bumping around aimlessly. Outside of life, she could be a butterfly, one that was uniquely magnificent and beautiful. She never watched theater, because she felt the wall between the stage and the audience was too flimsy. She couldn't convince herself to believe in it. So, it was only ever movies.
(Another voice: Excuse me, you don't seem to be talking about Swallowtail. Who are you talking about?)
It's always been Swallowtail. I haven't been talking about anyone else.
(Another voice: But it sounds like… you "knew" it.)
Hearty laughter
Yes. I knew her.

Recording Ends
ST_VisionArchives.C-7111Ob_RecordBeforeContent_2:
(Background noise)

…Who are you? What do you want? I don't do interviews.
(Another voice: We're not from the media.)
Hm? With all that equipment… Oh, is this about what happened before?

(Prolonged silence)

Come in, then. Don't just stand at the doorway.
(Another voice: Thanks for letting us in.)
What do you want to know?
(Another voice: Just tell us what happened.)
It was nothing special. On my way home from work, I was attacked by a vending machine that suddenly came to life. I was scared out of my wits when the president of the society appeared out of nowhere and effortlessly turned the vending machine into a Puka Sweet Dreams Marshmallow. I thought he was just a kind Esper passing by. When I thanked him, he told me it wasn't an Esper Ability. It was "magic." Espers can only nullify anomalies, but magic can do so much more. And he was just an ordinary person like me. As long as you study magic seriously, even ordinary people can do seemingly impossible things.
(Another voice: So you believed him?)
I was skeptical at first. But after following him to the society, I witnessed miracle after miracle.
(Another voice: "Miracles"?)
You might have other words for it. To me, they were miracles. At every gathering, he would present anomalies that had hurt people or nearly hurt people, and announce he would purify them with the power of magic. He'd draw a magic circle on the ground, and then the ground would glow. Those struggling anomalies would instantly transform into the most ordinary objects. He said this was the power of the Black Tome. The president of the society would casually perform these miracles like they were nothing, telling us that with enough practice, anyone could have this power… He was a bit odd, always muttering strange things, but he was easygoing. No matter when someone asked him about magic, he would set aside whatever he was doing and answer seriously. He reminded you of that friendly top student, or the helpful class representative… Anyway, he wasn't like what outsiders say.
(Another voice: Have you seen the Black Tome? What's written in it?)
I've seen it from a distance, but I've never read what's inside. Only the President could read that book. He said only "the chosen ones" could touch the tome, and it would be dangerous for anyone else to do so. Some people did try to steal the Black Tome when he wasn't paying attention. But I don't know why they all gave up in the end. The President often held that book and recited strange sentences, saying they were incantations. I copied down a few of them and practiced often.
(Another voice: Did the practice work?)
No. Of course not.

(Brief silence)

You've got the wrong person. I was just an ordinary follower of the Black Tome and the President. I never got close to either of them, and I didn't lose anything from this experience. During that incident… when the Black Tome went berserk and anomalies out of control took over the building, I wasn't hurt either.
To me, that time was like a dream. Every day I'd listen to the President talk about magic, then go home and give some serious practice. Every time I recited an incantation, nothing happened, but it never discouraged me. I just thought I wasn't skilled enough. If I had tried a little harder and became someone chosen by the Black Tome, I could've learned magic too. I really believed that.
I don't blame the President. Who goes through life without ever being deceived? "Everyone is unique and special"… Isn't that society's biggest lie?
…You should go. I have nothing more to say.

(Silence continues until the end of the recording)

ST_VisionArchives.OceanChase_VisionDescBefore:
R-1851(Or) is a large Bio Anomaly with an appearance similar to cetaceans, featuring ribbon-like flesh fins and tentacle-like aberrant organs on its surface, possibly a fusion of multiple marine organism characteristics. This Anomaly cannot be observed in real space, but instead operates within an Anomalous Realm whose entrance randomly appears near the undersea tunnel. All witnesses share the experience of suddenly entering the Anomalous Realm while driving through the undersea tunnel, and consistently report hearing complex calls resembling whale songs.
According to witness descriptions, this Anomalous Realm is a frozen wasteland connected to seas of blood, featuring surreal landscapes such as chains in the sky and giant ship anchors. Most witnesses chose to hide or exit their vehicles within the Anomalous Realm and were safely teleported back to the undersea tunnel. A very small number claim to have followed R-1851(Or) to the depths of the Anomalous Realm and were attacked by R-1851(Or). Historical records indicate that some Anomaly Hunter team disappearances may be connected to this Anomaly. Please handle with caution.
It is noteworthy that all interviewees, including those who encountered attacks, expressed varying degrees of concern and sympathy for R-1851(Or). It remains unclear whether this is due to the Anomaly's special abilities, the Anomalous Realm's influence on human emotions, or other reasons.
ST_VisionArchives.Lamp_RecordBefore_3:
XX/XX
Today I carried out an Eternal Lamp containment mission. Everything was going smoothly at first, and the containment was completed quickly. But for some reason, I had a momentary lapse in judgment and thought that draining the electricity from the lamp might be safer…
It exploded. Good thing there was more than one specimen…

XX/XX
I heard that an Eternal Lamp escaped from Zerogon Laboratory because of a small-scale power outage at the lab, which temporarily disabled its containment measures. I thought the lab's management was supposed to be really strict? In theory, there shouldn't be any power outages, right?
I asked a friend at the lab about the situation, and apparently it was because the Eternal Lamp consumed too much electricity that the lab couldn't pay the electric bill in time, which caused the blackout… Maybe it deliberately got itself caught just to enjoy the lab's free electricity?
I'm glad that re-containment quest wasn't assigned to me, I really have trauma from dealing with it…

XX/XX
Huh? I have to contain an Eternal Lamp again? Me? Wasn't it assigned to someone else before? Did that mission fail? Alright then…

ST_VisionArchives.Hospital_VisionDescAfter:
——█ █ █ FOR PREVIOUS INVESTIGATION PERSONNEL ONLY. DO NOT DISTRIBUTE. █ █ █——
Following review by ███, this Anomaly's classification has been elevated to Class V. This commission entry has been sealed, and related materials and editing permissions have been transferred to Yggash Court. Final interpretation rights for this entry belong to Yggash Court. Citation of any info from this entry is prohibited without written authorization.
This Anomaly is an abandoned large-scale medical facility known as Coldmount Hospital, presumed to exist in █████. The main structure is a four-story reinforced concrete building with unknown floor area. Time and space conditions within the facility are unstable, with potential chaotic overlaps. Various surge-type Anomalies are distributed throughout the floors, including U-6009-1(Or), some verified to possess aggressive or ██ threat capabilities. Additionally, the client suffers from dissociative amnesia and other psychiatric conditions of unknown origin.  Currently undergoing long-term treatment at Hethereau Municipal Hospital.
There is only one method for investigators to enter Coldmount Hospital: they must be affected by the client's Esper Ability to gain access, and this process is suspected to pose mental safety risks. Among the identified investigation personnel, approximately 60% reported experiencing aftereffects including auditory hallucinations, visual hallucinations, heart palpitations, nightmares, and other symptoms. Some individuals experienced organic damage, and a very few ██.
Regarding the abandonment of Coldmount Hospital, multiple investigators claim to have collected important documents within the facility, but neither original nor transcribed copies could be removed from that space in any form. Investigators can only relay contents based on vague memories. Multiple investigators mentioned that "an Anomaly incident occurred" before the facility's abandonment, which may have important connections to the hospital's abandonment and the appearance of U-6009-1(Or), but event details remain unclear.
After comprehensive verification, no medical facility named Coldmount Hospital or with a similar architectural layout has been found, nor are there any Anomaly incident records matching "██" characteristics. All phenomena, entities, and documented files from this Anomaly facility show no historical or logical connections to the real world.
***If you experience any phantom limb pain, skin burning sensations, or psychological dependence on bandages, please remain calm, cease all physical contact activities with others, and immediately contact the Bureau of Anomaly Control or Anomaly Hunter Guild. Qualified personnel will provide diagnostic and consultation services.
ST_VisionArchives.OceanChase_RecordBefore_3:
…
A whale's vocal organs, the fins and tail of bony fish, the arms of jellyfish… That isn't a creature from this world. It's many life symbols stacked together, a warning from all the living beings of this ocean.
As for those chains appearing out of nowhere, the abnormally sized ship anchors, and that blood-red sea… I can't find a scientific explanation (well, that's pretty common in Hethereau). Anyway, even if just for the safety of the undersea tunnel, this is definitely a subject worth studying.
…
Those idiots in the meeting have absolutely no standards, jumping to conclusions just from hearing one-sided accounts from a few scared Anomaly Hunters! If they'd seen it with their own eyes, they would never say something as stupid as "a beast thirsting for revenge." Its rhythmic whale songs are clearly signs of friendliness. If they can't understand that, it's their problem. But what's with those frenzied attack behaviors…? This is my area of expertise. I'll figure it out.
…
I tried strapping two large speakers to my car roof and playing whale calls while heading to the Anomalous Realm passage. I'm a genius. It responded clearly in a friendly manner, showing curiosity. If I'm reading it right, this friendship plan was a success.
…
It's always the same… After being in the Anomalous Realm for a while, the seawater starts turning red, anchors and chains fall from the sky, and then you start attacking everything around you out of control… But why? Are you venting your anger? Is this a manifestation of your nightmares? If that's the case, why do you look so pained…? How can I help…?
…
Damn it, I finally figured it out. There's a damn harpoon stuck in your back. Something's very wrong with it. That's definitely not an ordinary object, at least not anymore. I strongly suspect that's also an Anomaly… Maybe that's the cause of all this? I'll find a way to fix it.
…
I've made up my mind. This will be the most dangerous thing I've ever done in my life…
I'm going to meet you either as a hero or a fool, blasting whale song symphonies through my speakers… Then I'll climb onto your body and pull out that eyesore of a harpoon, or dig it out, or nullify it, and finally turn the seawater here blue again! Whatever it takes, there's got to be a way.
Here's to your freedom! Here's to my success!
ST_VisionArchives.OceanChase_RecordBefore_2:
First, let me clarify that I am not accepting this interview in any official capacity.
Additionally, I hope your records will use precise terminology and avoid biased content that might mislead the public.
Let me start with my conclusion. Personally, I believe this Anomaly has enormous destructive potential and poses significant threats, but it is not the type to actively hunt humans. If you accidentally enter the Anomalous Realm, you can safely exit by quickly getting out of your vehicle.
I refuse to answer that question. Most Anomaly Hunters are not at the level required to contain it. Do not attempt the challenge recklessly.
I was driving normally through the undersea tunnel when I heard whale sounds. I immediately recalled records about this Anomaly and began maintaining vigilance. After reaching a specific location, I felt the vehicle jolt, visibility dropped sharply, and the whale calls became much closer. I determined that I had entered the Anomalous Realm.
Then it appeared, but showed no hostility. Instead, it swept over my head and opened a glowing passage ahead… as if guiding me forward. I didn't slow down, instead driving into that frozen wasteland, following it to reach the center of the Anomalous Realm.
If you insist on asking… there was some combat, I suppose.
As I was about to reach the depths of the Anomalous Realm, the whale began making different sounds. I could sense that it's becoming uncontrolled, agitated, emitting very harsh… calls. Then it began attacking me.
Its calls… I believe that poses no harm, at least it didn't interfere with my reactions and judgment… No, strictly speaking, it did have some effect on my condition, but it wasn't direct interference. Rather, it induced some… distracting feelings of sorrow.
It was calling to me for help.
ST_VisionArchives.Boombox_RecordBefore_3:
…You heard right, that equipment really is mine. When I first got into electronic music at Clement Academy, and during my early commercial work, it was always by my side. I thought my agent had thrown it away, but it turned out it became an Anomaly and came back here… I'm truly ashamed.
Actually, I'm an Esper. You could say that when I compose, I can hear the "voices" of instruments and equipment.
I've been obsessed with video game music since I was little, and when I started creating my own music, I'd always incorporate those elements. Even my stage name ties back to it! In my early works, those unique sounds were like my personal touch and signature, and "they" loved it too. We explored music creation together, discussing and perfecting the works we were proud of, which brought us to where we are today… but also where we stopped…
After I was signed to a music company, I often had to perform at big music festivals and corporate events, or work on soundtracks for films and TV shows. The clients all disliked those sounds that seemed outdated and cheap, and pushed back against my street vibes. At first, I was rebellious. I ignored the company's objections and stuck to my style, believing that great work would eventually be recognized. Then, at a major event, I presented our painstakingly crafted new piece and raised my hands during the climax…
But there was no reaction from the audience. No one cared about our carefully crafted rhythms and melodies, no one stood up to cheer, no one swayed their bodies, and… no one showed even the slightest bit of excitement in their eyes. The audience just gave polite applause, then whispered among themselves, occasionally letting out condescending snickers… That day, I couldn't finish the performance. I left the stage hastily and sealed that equipment away in my mansion's basement… along with everything from my past.

Sorry for making you listen to all this self-serving talk. In the end, I actively betrayed who I was, and I betrayed them… all for better opportunities. There's no arguing with that. I'm glad they chose to return there, back to the place where we used to create our beloved works together. I can never go back.
…Also, I came to you with one more request.
If it comes to the point where you have to deal with it, please record and preserve its music completely before you contain… or nullify it.
Its voice shouldn't be silenced.
ST_VisionArchives.BuildingDrawing_Record_3:
Those blueprints and that messy building facade in the Anomalous Realm… there's more to them than meets the eye.
Anyone in architectural design should know whose work that is, or rather, which group of people were behind it.
Back then, during Hethereau's high-rise and commercial district development phase, some developers hyped up a concept: they would design all the building facades on the commercial street as one unified plane, allowing them to project massive advertisements. It caused quite a stir at the time. An old-school architectural design scholar took the lead in publicly opposing it, believing that architectural design should serve citizens and the urban landscape, not advertisment for these big corporations.
It's normal that you don't know about it. After all, that concept never actually came to fruition. It was just an attention-grabbing gimmick at the end of the day… But that stubborn old gentleman didn't stop there. He kept attacking the concept, and eventually the entire design industry… One day, he suddenly took extended leave with no campus courses or projects… Eventually, he quietly left the design academy.
That's right. Many people suspected he faced some… pressure from the industry, but no one really knows the truth. Angry students wanted to figure out what happened and tried to contact him, but got no response. They attempted to investigate through the school, but were only met with delays and dismissal.
But in the end, they found an envelope that hadn't been taken away, stuck in a gap in the scholar's office desk drawer. Inside was a roughly sketched design drawing showing the entire commercial street, with every building's facade covered in uneven, unsightly structures. Even the worst designer wouldn't do something like that. No one knew if it was the scholar's work, or what it was trying to convey… But as you've seen, those blueprints that became Anomalies, and that building in the Anomalous Realm, they all inherited this incomprehensible design… It's their kind of secret code, and their revenge against this city, against all cities. If you see any building with this kind of design, it proves that some lucky guy succeeded.
"Spatial art"? Hahaha… I wonder who invented such a far-fetched term. The word "art" sure is convenient…
But compared to the orderly cubes packed with cities and covered in advertisements, I'd rather see more of these ugly "artworks."
ST_VisionArchives.ElevatorAnomaly_01_Record_2:
Inquiry Feedback Record Regarding the Bureau Elevator Anomaly Destruction Incident

Phone call recording transcript

Because it happened about 3 minutes before rush hour.
…No, I wasn't in the elevator. I didn't leave my room. I was just watching the security cameras.
Based on my calculations at the time, disregarding other costs, the fastest and most fundamental solution to the problem was to immediately send the elevator crashing from the top floor to the bottom floor. Destroy it.
…
Because using broadcasts to notify people, then sealing off the area and going through standard Nullification procedures would have been too inefficient.
Sorry, I'm not good at explaining over the phone. I've already put the file on your desktop.

(Attachment: cause.txt)

Internal Note A: So the property damage this time was confirmed to be caused by that shut-in Captain? Wait, you actually dared to call them directly?!
Reply: Once they started talking, their attitude was actually okay… And they answered all the questions.
Internal Note B: Why do you have their number?
Reply: I complained to an online friend about it, and they gave it to me. Said I could reach the culprit with this number. Pretty impressive, right?
Internal Note C: Add the follow-up and conclusions. Fraxinus needs confirmation.
Reply: It seems to specifically target elevators, randomly transforming them into Anomalous Realm entrances. Two solutions: destroy the Anomalous Realm the entrance leads to, or destroy the entrance itself. Normally, we choose the former to be safe, but that means taking on the risk of exploring whatever random Anomalous Realm appears beyond the elevator each time. The time and workload required… it may not be less than reinstalling an elevator. As for the latter, setting aside the financial loss… as of now, the newly installed elevator in the same location has not exhibited this Anomaly again.
Internal Note D: The reasoning is perfectly organized, the actions seem extreme no matter how you look at it, yet the outcome is actually OK. What even is this…
ST_VisionArchives.Anomaly0163_RecordBeforeContent_3:
We've got some clues about the unusual length of Doomscroll videos.
Take the recently popular "After School" as an example. You might have heard of it; it's about a protagonist trapped in the school building after school with "friends", who eventually finds a way home after many attempts.
Following the rules of the "Red Light, Green Light" game while overcoming obstacles to find a way out of the school. Your "friends" will catch you if you're not careful, and all your efforts will be in vain. No wonder the protagonist keeps returning to the start, repeating the cycle until the lengthy video ends, right?
However, our research confirms that the normal length of this movie is just a few minutes. The extended versions circulating on social media were deliberately edited to repeat the trial and error cycles, creating the impression of endlessness.
Who has the power to edit Anomaly Videos? Could this be their Asper Ability? Why do they do this? These questions require further investigation.
ST_VisionArchives.Anomaly0163_VisionDescBefore: Doomscroll is an Anomaly in the form of video that had spread widely on social media, hijacking the internet. Viewers become engrossed in the video within seconds. In the early stages of attention being captured by Doomscroll (usually within the first minute), one can still escape the video's allure and control through self-discipline. Once deeply engrossed, it becomes impossible to voluntarily break away from the video's pull until the video ends. Fortunately, this peculiar attraction only affects first-time viewers. For those who've already watched the video, it's no different from any other ordinary video.

ST_VisionArchives.NiKanDao_VisionDescBefore:
"What You See" originated from the work of a brilliant artist who recognized both the deceptive nature of paintings and the deceptive nature of our own eyes. Building upon this discovery, he created numerous wonderful images filled with optical illusions in his works.
Thus, the Anomaly "What You See" was born on the canvas of one of the artist's paintings. The canvas connects the world on paper with the real world, constructing a new "canvas" within the observer's vision. When the observer becomes aware of the connection between the painting and reality, they are drawn into its strange Anomalous Realm.
The artist who originally created these anomalous paintings has passed away. His works from his lifetime are scattered around the world, and all of these paintings possess anomalous properties. People are often drawn into the anomalous realm because of them.

The Rain-sweeping Maid is originally a gentle Anomaly with an instinct to clear away rainwater. They rest on sunny days and become energized in the rain, eagerly beginning their work by absorbing rainwater into their bodies for temporary storage. Then, they seek out rivers to release the water once the skies clear. Perhaps because they carry humanity's wishes for fair weather, the Rain-sweeping Maid firmly believe their actions make rainy days pass more quickly.
However, after absorbing contaminated rainwater, the Rain-sweeping Maid lose control of their behavior. Tormented by the tainted water, they can no longer drain properly on their own. Instead, they can only repeat an endless cycle of releasing black rain and reabsorbing it, creating an Anomalous Realm of dark clouds and upward-flowing rain around themselves. An uncontrolled Rain-sweeping Maid will swing its tail, resembling a vacuum hose, launching indiscriminate attacks on any creature that wanders into its rain curtain, just as it once drove away storm clouds, until the intruder is driven out of range.
During the process of releasing and reabsorbing rainwater, if the surrounding temperature drops sharply, the Rain-sweeping Maid's rain will change with the natural environment, condensing into freezing rain, hail, or snowflakes, transforming the rain curtain into a localized blizzard. Humans who enter the blizzard will also be attacked. In short, whether in the heat of summer or the depths of winter, if you see a single patch of dark clouds under an otherwise clear sky, be careful. There is most likely a Rain-sweeping Maid struggling in agony within.

ST_VisionArchives.Anomaly0030_RecordBeforeContent_2:
Inspiration Terminators don't just steal one idea—they seem to feed on all related thoughts.
I came to this conclusion based on my own experience, though it's still embarrasing:
After sending my manuscript to my editor, I tried writing a spinoff since I couldn't relax. That's when an Inspiration Terminator struck.
It felt like slamming the brakes on a speeding train. I couldn't remember anything about my main story either, and sounded like an idiot when my editor called…
Only after hiring an Anomaly Hunter did my nightmare end, and my manuscript finally came back to life. Reflecting on it, the spinoff's setting and plot were extensions of the main story. So, when an Inspiration Terminator strikes, it doesn't just block your current idea—it suppresses all related thoughts and concepts too.
Looks like I'll need more insecticide for my next writing session.

"Sir, in your report you mentioned encountering an anomaly with a red door and noticing something unusual. Could you elaborate on that?"
"Oh ho ho! Patience, young one. Let me tell you… It was high noon precisely. I was calculating my afternoon sales when—ah, but I mustn't reveal heaven's secrets. Anyway, I packed up my stall and headed to Hankaku Street…"
"The anomaly was sighted during the day, near Hankaku Street."
"Noon! It was noon! You youngsters are so careless. Lucky you have me to set you straight."
"The witness emphasizes the time as noon. Whether this is a crucial factor remains to be determined."
"As I walked, I suddenly couldn't move forward. The path was completely blocked, not even a crack to squeeze through!"
"You see, young one, those who interpret heaven's will, value the path we walk above all. Encountering an anomaly is a destined path. If heaven wills it, how can I not obey? Even if it led to certain doom, I had to press on!"
"While I may not match you Anomaly Hunters in strength, I can certainly fend for myself. That space beyond the door, it seemed real, but it was merely a projection of another world. One misstep and you'd be lost, becoming a meal for the creatures inside. But I, with my years of experience and my prized possession that sharpens the mind and clears the vision…"
"Excuse me, JTF stands for Joint Task Force."
"I'm basically a half-dead man! It's only natural I don't know all your acronyms and codes. Now, where was I?"
"You mentioned that the Anomalous Realm you saw wasn't truly real. That's quite an interesting observation. Could you expand on that?"
"Tch… Let me ask you this. This anomaly has both red and blue doors, inside and out. What's the meaning behind that? You all know the red door in the wall connects to the real world, but the blue doors link the virtual spaces… That's the key! I have an item that can discern truth from falsehood. The closer to the red door, the more it vibrates, like a strong pulse. But near the blue doors, it's still as death. What does this tell us? That world inside is entirely fake! The disappearing school building, reliving campus days—it's all a beautiful dream conjured by some work-shy youngster, playing right into that man-eating world's hands! If I were it, I'd put on such a false front to lure people in too… Thanks to my precious prayer beads, I escaped unscathed, not devoured by the Oddities inside! Our meeting today was fated. I see your destiny is intertwined with it. I'm willing to part with this treasure, to perfect this destined encounter. In exchange for some Fons… (Advertisement content removed)"
"…Thank you for your information."
(The anomaly space inside the Red Door resembling a school building scenario is suspected to be a "mirage" manifesting in response to people's thoughts, not a real school building that ever existed… Although this citizen friend said a lot, the amount of useful information extracted is not substantial. I suspect this is a story he made up to sell that magical bracelet… But what if it's not? For instance, if that bracelet really is an anomaly that can see through falsehoods? Uh, should I really buy it?)

ST_VisionArchives.Lamp_VisionDescBefore:

This Anomaly commonly appears in nighttime alleyways, stealing electricity from the surrounding area. When it manifests, the surrounding region experiences complete power outages accompanied by spreading black fog, plunging entire city blocks into darkness and significantly disrupting the daily lives of nearby residents. It's quite common nowadays to inadvertently come across Doomscroll. Personally, I don't feel it affects me much.
Maybe it's because I'm used to watching things at 2x or even 4x speed, I can't even remember the last time I sat down and watched a movie. Not just for me—most people probably think there's no need for it, right? After all, the content you want to see has mostly been edited into those "OOXX SUMMARIZED IN 5 MINUTES" short videos that you can click on anytime. It's okay not to focus too much on the screen, as there are summaries and key points neatly explained, like fast food fed into a tube that connects to your mind. In short, just a few minutes of video can give you the gist of the story, perfect for casual conversation. However, due to the nature of Doomscroll, I can actually watch several Anomaly Videos, all focused. It's a refreshing experience.
These videos' plots could use more excitement. If you're unlucky enough to watch a boring one, having to see it from start to finish is quite unbearable.

Don't you think some neighbors have absolutely no sense of decency? Their pipes are broken, but since it doesn't affect their own home, they just leave it be. Meanwhile, everyone downstairs suffers! Murky black water is seeping through the ceiling and dripping down! Disgusting, right?
I heard their household habits are terrible. They leave in the morning, forgetting to turn off the faucet. Combined with that pipe they never fixed, it's the perfect recipe for disaster! The poor victims downstairs are constantly flooded, the walls are all moldy, and the floors are completely ruined!
Tell me, what are these people trying to do leaving the faucet running all day? Go for a swim? Wash their car indoors?…Or, maybe they're a mermaid reincarnated? Insisting on living on land for some… deeply moving, tearjerking reason? Grr, if they need that much water to live, they should just move into an aquarium!
Huh? You're asking about an Anomaly? What Anomaly?
…Oh, there's an Anomaly in the community elevator? Bah, I wouldn't know about that. I live in the villa district.
ST_VisionArchives.PObⅡS-5701_RecordAfter02:
Had to square off with those two rowdy fists to protect everyone!
The most distinct thing about them was this… protein powder smell… But after the scuffle, they smelled kinda burnt, perhaps from overexcitement.
They were stronger than I thought! And just when I was circling for a weak spot, the ring heated up, and those fading fists got a second wind.
Must be some ring battle rule. Can't let my guard down—not even for a sec! Well, I learned my lesson. Next time I'll wrap it up quickly!
ST_VisionArchives.OceanChase_VisionDescAfter:
A large Bio Anomaly with a whale as its primary body, featuring multiple aberrant organs along its sides and abdomen, possibly formed from scar tissue mutations after trauma. The back displays an elongated metallic protrusion, confirmed to be the rear end of an antique harpoon, with the middle and front sections deeply embedded in the whale's torso. Expert analysis suggests this harpoon resembles components from ship-mounted heavy whaling cannons, though its size significantly exceeds all historically documented equipment of similar type. The Anomaly is theorized to have transformed from a whale that perished during historical whaling activities, while the harpoon within synchronously converted into a parasitic Anomaly designated R-1851-1(Ob). It should be noted that unlike typical accompanying or subordinate relationships, the coexistence mode between the harpoon and whale more closely resembles parasitism.
R-1851(Or) possesses anomalous abilities, capable of creating a narrow passage connecting Anomalous Realms to actual ocean areas, and sings whale songs in the passage to influence selected vehicle drivers, luring them into the passage to go into the Anomalous Realm with it. Within the passage, this Anomaly exhibits relatively calm behavior, with some investigators reporting they could sense it attempting to communicate with them. However, after entering the Anomalous Realm, R-1851(Or) sometimes suddenly displays intense repetitive behaviors, accompanied by piercing wails, and begins attacking objects within the Anomalous Realm or the investigators themselves in an uncontrolled manner. The cause remains currently unknown.
One hypothesis suggests that the Anomalous Realm inhabited by R-1851(Or) was not generated by it. The internal ship anchors, chains, seas of blood, and urban landscapes are more likely connected to R-1851-1(Ob). R-1851-1(Ob) may have transformed into an Anomaly earlier than R-1851(Or), possessing strong tendencies toward control, imprisonment, and abuse behaviors, and created this Anomalous Realm to imprison and torture the whale it struck but failed to kill. Eventually, the whale transformed into an Anomaly and began luring humans into this space through various means, seeking to end its prolonged suffering. This theory remains unverified and can never be verified.
ST_VisionArchives.Boss33_CusConmment_3_Dis_Player:
A Bio Anomaly that lures lost children into its nest. Once it succeeds, it never allows its "children" to leave. It views anyone attempting to rescue the children as thieves trying to steal them away, and launches vicious attacks against them.
To minimize harm, Anomaly Hunters should head to the nest of the Nestbound Bird the moment it is discovered. The longer the delay, the greater the chance of children falling victim. We must never let the worst-case scenario happen again. The threat must be eliminated early to prevent disaster before it strikes.
ST_VisionArchives.Boss33_CusConmment_1_Dis_Player:
A Bio Anomaly that lures lost children into its nest. Once it succeeds, it never allows its "children" to leave. It views anyone attempting to rescue the children as thieves trying to steal them away, and launches vicious attacks against them.

ST_VisionArchives.Boss33_CusConmment_2_Dis_Player:
A Bio Anomaly that lures lost children into its nest. Once it succeeds, it never allows its "children" to leave. It views anyone attempting to rescue the children as thieves trying to steal them away, and launches vicious attacks against them.

ST_VisionArchives.Anomaly0118_RecordAfter:
The so-called king of racers… Headless Rider… Didn't bother to inquire before coming here. This street, this road, this Hethereau, is under the protection of my the Coluccis. Daring to bully my underlings on my turf?
Well, my underlings took me, the Ichi-daime boss, on a patrol, and it immediately took the bait. The scythe and motorcycle entrance were pretty cool, with the blue flames looking intense, but it was just superficially intimidating. I've seen far more terrifying Espers in my time!
However, this anomaly suited my taste; it didn't have too many twists and turns. In a fight… uh… it was no match for me at all! I considered recruiting it into the family, riding a motorcycle with a scythe, looking like the main character. But it couldn't communicate… sigh… "Judge of the Night Racers" sounds pretty cool, doesn't it? It's almost a shame it got nullified like that…
ST_VisionArchives.C-7111Ob_RecordBeforeContent_3:
Ever since I was little, I believed I was special. I had great grades, many talents, and my athletic abilities weren't bad either. Parents, neighbors, teachers, classmates… everyone liked me. My life was like a game on easy mode. I could effortlessly grind to max level and breeze through the newbie village. I was convinced I was the MC of a manga, who wielded the power of gods and anime.
But that sense of superiority vanished after I transferred schools. At my old school, I was firmly seated at the top of my grade. But here, even studying until dawn barely got me to average. The skills I once took pride in were just beginner-level here. What made it more hopeless was that the harder I tried, the more I realized how ordinary I was. Even in the napping club, I couldn't fall asleep as fast or sleep as the others.
…What's with that look? Ha, of course you normies wouldn't understand. Being an Esper is such a special, incredible thing. You don't have to do anything, don't have to put in any effort, and you get powers that ordinary people could never achieve in a lifetime.
But I still believed I had to be special. Even after all those setbacks, even standing at the foot of the mountain looking up at the glory of geniuses, I still felt that way. Because I was the center of the world. The world revolved around me. Isn't that how it works in manga? The true Savior is always the most unremarkable person in the crowd at first. So everything I was going through was just a trial from destiny. That's right, there are many geniuses, each in their own field. I just hadn't found my own unique talent yet. Once my talent awakened, everything would fall into place.
And then, I really did find it.
The first time I heard about the Black Tome was on some urban legend website that's no longer running. Before anomalies entered the public eye, we called all phenomena that couldn't be explained by science "magic." Unlike Esper Abilities, magic wasn't some lofty power monopolized by a select few. Someone like me, as long as I worked hard enough, could master that incredible power. This was the call of destiny I had been searching for. My calling.
After obtaining the Black Tome, everything that followed felt natural. At first, it was disappointed that I was still weak, not to mention the so-called incantations written in it did nothing whatsoever. But soon, I discovered that if I fed it low threat anomalies, it would quickly grow and become all-powerful. And even more efficient than low threat anomalies, what it craved most, was human faith. Of course I had faith in it, but just me alone was meaningless.
Hm? Yes, that's when I started the secret society. Back then, I was probably completely blinded by it. All I could think about was holding onto this hard-won power tighter and tighter, making myself its one and only master until the end of times… I wouldn't allow anyone to covet this power. Nonetheless, to grow the Black Tome's followers and strengthen its power, my power, I deceived many people with pretty words. People just like me.
I made a terrible mistake. Thankfully, no one was hurt in that incident. Otherwise, I really would have regretted it for the rest of my life. No, the responsibility of deceiving and using all those people is already enough to carry for a lifetime.
I understand now. Not everyone is special. Not me, not you, not anyone. Even Espers might only have the ability to move a spoon by telekinesis. Throughout all of history, there have been very few people truly chosen by destiny. Many people in this world believe they are special, to the point that such belief has become commonplace. I am but one with the masses. After all these years, after committing such a serious mistake, after taking such a long detour, I'm finally willing to admit it.
…After I got out of the detention center, I saw the faces of my parents and my friends as they waited for my release… I'll never forget them as long as I live.
It might sound strange coming from me, but this is truly how I feel now. I don't need Esper Abilities, magic, the Black Tome, or lies. I don't need to be special. I can still live a good life.

ST_VisionArchives.BPhⅡE-0085_VisionDesBefore:
Accompanying the water columns flowing down from the sky to this place are intangible, semi-transparent carps. According to long-standing rules, these carps can only return to the sky after completing a specific trial, temporarily ending this Anomaly.

Occasionally, citizens are drawn to this dreamlike spectacle, and upon discovering that the wandering carps have no ill intentions, they approach. It is important to note their strong instinctive drive to challenge the Dragon Gate. When they cannot find the Dragon Gate, they will turn to other forms of challenges with passerbys..

Although in ancient times, the Dragon Gate trials were typically elaborate song and dance ceremonies, nowadays, this phenomenon occurs quite frequently, and there is no luxury to handle it elegantly and peacefully every time..

ST_VisionArchives.PPhⅠS-13_VisionDescAfter:
As a Phenomenon Anomaly, this Anomaly attaches to an open box, appearing as a black open box with a yellow letter "C" on it. Once attached, it typically spawns other box-like objects that float around the main body, which is considered the most direct way to identify this Anomaly. When Proliferative C detects signs of activity from other living beings within a certain range, it reacts by manifesting large numbers of box-like objects out of thin air to block others from approaching Proliferative C. Attempting to close Proliferative C may provoke its attacks, primarily through ramming with its main body and generating various types of boxes for offensive purposes. After successfully closing it, Proliferative C will revert to its original form.
Investigation reveals that Proliferative C can attach to any box that has remained unsealed for an extended period, whether it's a cardboard box, shipping container, or even a figurine box. If left unattended for too long, these boxes will disappear from their original location and reappear in other corners of the city. Considering the potential contents within Proliferative C, operations on the main body during the nullification process should be conducted carefully, and it's recommended to record the operation through filming or other documentation methods to avoid potential disputes. After nullification is complete, please contact the Security Office, which will handle the subsequent process of locating the original owner.

ST_VisionArchives.Anomaly0094_RecordBeforeContent_1:
I've encountered what you're talking about on my way to work.
I remember it crystal clear. It was the day I overslept after binge-watching a series all night. Thinking "I'm going to be late!" I took a shortcut I rarely use. As I was rushing towards 2-Four, lamenting that I'd probably kiss my punctuality bonus goodbye this month, that thing appeared.
Yeah, it was similar to what others have seen. The trash can in the alley suddenly came to life, joining with many others that flew in from who knows where, forming a wall of trash cans right in front of me! There was even one with our store's label on it. I reckon it was the one from the back door.
Along with the trash cans came that red door, comically filling in a gap in the trash can wall. It creaked open with a squeak. By the way, whenever I see a door open, I can't help but want to say, "Welcome!"
But no matter how welcoming that door might be, I wasn't going in… Who knows where it leads? I've heard that others who went through ended up coming out from the other side of the wall. But I wasn't about to risk my perfect attendance bonus for that.
Speaking of which, when the manager heard I encountered an anomaly from the sky blocking the way and had to take a big detour, they approved my late arrival that day without deducting my bonus. Is this a blessing in disguise?

ST_VisionArchives.BPhⅡE-0085_Record_3:
Regarding that video of the Anomaly with many carp streamers flying down from the sky… or should I say River Anomaly.
Honestly, I don't understand what those who like that Anomaly are amazed by, and some even want to go see it in person. Please, if it's just because you think the scene is beautiful, can't CG animation technology achieve the same thing? Isn't this common in movies?
Statements like "life is beautiful" or "thankful for the gift" almost made me think I walked into a fool's sanctuary instead of a comment section. Did anyone expect to do some greening on top of those reinforced concrete buildings? Isn't that just creating trouble?

And speaking of the much-talked-about "Trial of the Dragon Gate", it made me feel that there are an unusually large number of people who are being played without realizing it.
First of all, these fish are semi-transparent, you can see it if you look closely, right? They have no physical form, right? You actually can't block them because they can completely pass through your body, and most attacks can't possibly harm them, right?
They can jump over if they want, and continue the fight if they wish, but they deliberately act as if they can be blocked by humans, as if they're truly undergoing some kind of trial…
Oh? So we use a bunch of manpower to put on a show and play around with them, being careful not to block them too perfunctorily lest they succeed—when clearly, if they wanted to succeed, no one could stop them? Two kids squabbling in the neighborhood entrance is more of a back-and-forth struggle than this, right? What is this?
Is it impossible to understand without explaining it clearly? So many people play along with the Anomaly and then praise it as cute, which amuses me because, in the Anomaly's eyes, you're the one who's adorably foolish.

In the end, isn't it just the same old Malicious Anomaly behavior? Forcing humans to comply with its rules, punishing those who don't.
Ah, I get it—so as long as the form looks good and there's a bit of sweetness, everyone will think it's a "good" anomaly.
Even the fact that this anomaly has harmed many can be conveniently forgotten. Now, hit me with the "Ohhhh don't be such a grumpy conspiracy theorist!" Which is fine! From now on, everything will be viewed from a positive angle, interpreted in a good light! Such positivity! Much love! Wowzers!
Ignorance really is bliss, huh.
ST_VisionArchives.ZhangYuChe_VisionDescBefore: An oddity with decent camouflage abilities that occasionally appears on roads throughout Hethereau in the form of an old trailer truck with octopus tentacles. Under normal circumstances, Octowpus will try its best to follow traffic rules to blend into its surroundings, but there are also cases where Octowpus attacks nearby pedestrians and facilities. Since it's impossible to predict when it will attack, citizens are advised to keep their distance once they spot Octowpus.

ST_VisionArchives.Lamp_RecordBefore_2:
When my senior assigned me the Eternal Lamp containment quest, they told me it was just a really simple task, so I didn't think much of it. By the time I got to the quest location it was already pretty late, and I figured I'd grab some late-night snacks from the convenience store first… But when I came to my senses, the whole area was covered in thick fog! Plus the streetlights were flickering on and off, and some weren't working at all.
In theory… in theory none of that should be scary… but I had just watched this horror movie that was also set on dark streets, and remembering those scenes suddenly made me super, super scared! Oh, but I'm not scared anymore! Movies are just movies!
As for the actual containment quest… a few lights appeared in the black fog, and some humanoid figures approached… I knew those were Eternal Lamps, but I really made a mistake! I was so terrified that I forgot I was supposed to contain them, and I got a bit too heavy-handed and ended up nullifying them all…
Ah, after I nullified them, the power in the area was restored immediately.
Oh right, and the steamed buns at that nearby convenience store taste really good!

ST_VisionArchives.BuildingDrawing_VisionDescBefore:
An Object Anomaly originating from engineering blueprints, capable of floating and moving through the air with autonomous behavioral abilities. It has been sighted multiple times at a construction site, with its activity centered around a building under construction at that location.
This Anomaly appears to exhibit active human-trapping behavior, attracting targets by displaying blueprints and rapidly expanding to envelop them when they approach, subsequently teleporting them to its Anomalous Realm. According to firsthand accounts, the Anomalous Realm's periphery contains numerous building clusters resembling hand-drawn sketches, while the central area features a uniquely designed tower similar in scale to the building under construction at the site, though with a different design.
To date, all witnesses who entered this Anomalous Realm have safely returned within one hour. Some witnesses claim to have attempted climbing the tower's unique external structures and discovered talking design blueprints. After reading these blueprints, they felt the surrounding space undergo distorted changes, though this caused them no harm or negative effects.
ST_VisionArchives.BuildingDrawing_VisionDescAfter:
An Object Anomaly originating from discarded engineering design blueprints, capable of floating and moving through the air with autonomous behavioral abilities. The designs in the blueprints point to the building where it resides, though this proposal was abandoned during the architectural design phase.
This Anomaly exhibits active human-trapping behavior, attracting targets by displaying blueprints and rapidly expanding to envelop them when they approach, subsequently teleporting them to its Anomalous Realm. This space appears to be a three-dimensional projection of design sketches, with hand-drawn sketch-style building clusters on the periphery and a building matching the blueprint design at the center. The Anomaly disperses itself into multiple blueprints that wait throughout the building, with some blueprints capable of granting readers the ability to distort space, though the activation conditions remain unclear. To date, all witnesses who entered the Anomalous Realm have safely returned within one hour.
It's worth noting that construction of this building came to a temporary halt during the building period, with changes in both design and construction teams. According to reports, the building's original design proposal was abandoned due to its overly distinctive style, which caused strong dissatisfaction among the design team. The original architect once climbed the unfinished building in protest and was ultimately expelled and dismissed from their position.
