ST_VisionArchives.BPhⅡE-0085_CusComment_3_Dis_Player: The Anomaly known as "Tidal Ascension" is actually water columns cascading from the heavens. The phantom "Fish Streamers" are a part of this phenomenon… or perhaps, they could be considered mere ornaments? To them, a battle is nothing more than a ritualistic "trial." Once it is concluded, they vanish, leaving no actual damage in their wake. In nature, most fish die during their migration or upon reaching their destination. Yet these immortal "Fish Streamers" seem to exist solely to nurture and sustain the cycle of life. It's truly a curious thing…
ST_VisionArchives.Boss33_Record_3:
I've heard that some people go out of their way to find the Nestbound Bird's nest, hoping to score some treasure. Doesn't the story go that the Nestbound Bird was so busy collecting gold and silver thread for its nest that it neglected its own children? That nest must be overflowing with jewels and riches!
Pah, only someone who's never dealt with the Nestbound Bird would believe such nonsense. One look inside its nest and you'll know the truth.
There's nothing there but despair.
Maybe that's a bit dramatic. Let me put it this way: the only materials used to build that nest are emptiness and heartbreak. Anyone who's heard that bird's mournful, pitiful cries would find it hard not to shed a tear. Even so, we can't show it any mercy. We must carry out Nullification, for the sake of all the families it has torn apart, for all the children who lost themselves after being lured away.
…
And for my own child.

Maybe I'm the only one who thinks this way: to carry out Nullification, to end its suffering… perhaps that too is a form of kindness.
ST_VisionArchives.Boss33_Record_1:
Whoa! I never knew the stories mom told me weren't just to scare me. They're real!
I've actually met that thing! That day, I had a fight with mom and ran away from home without even eating lunch. I was gonna hide at grandpa's place, but I got lost… When I came to my senses, I found myself in a really dark place for some reason, with thick fog all around. I couldn't see anything! It was so quiet there, except for some weird bird calls every now and then. It gave me the creeps… So scary!
Then I heard it calling me. It sounded just like mom, telling me to come home because it was dangerous outside. I said "okay" without thinking. The next second, a huge claw grabbed me! I was so scared I shut my eyes and screamed… When I was put down again, I was in a place that looked like a bird's nest. The thing that brought me there was a big bird wearing a mask, and it wrapped its wings around me. I peeked through the gaps in its feathers, and the nest was all dark and creepy too. There was a really, really big egg in the middle. I thought it was the big bird's baby egg, but it was already broken…
The big bird spoke, and it sounded exactly like the voice in the fog. It told me to stay with it forever, to stay with mommy. I said, "You're not my mom though?" Then it got really angry. Suddenly, someone burst in from outside, so I shouted, "Save me!" He rescued me and even gave me some mochi to eat. The mochi was cold, but it was yummy.
Hm? What happened in between? He told me not to look because I'm just a kid, so I didn't. I'm a good kid.
ST_VisionArchives.PObⅠS-7605_RecordAfter:
Yeah, that thing, what's it called again? You know, the thing that plays videos. Ah, never mind, it's not important. It might not pack a punch, but it's full of surprises—might as well call it the Enigma Anomaly! Or how about the Test-Your-Patience Anomaly? I'd rather duke it out than snooze through its shenanigans!
Me? I like to take it easy, let the films roll, and beat up whatever comes my way—that usually does the trick!

ST_VisionArchives.Sadbear_RecordBefore_2:
Yeah, yeah, I ran into it while delivering packages. Wow, that Anomaly Hunter was so pitiful, getting chased around everywhere by a big bear doll, so I stepped in to lend a hand. Its armor was actually super sturdy! Luckily, Lady Haniel with her incredible eyesight spotted its weakness right away. I saw a black shadow streak across two pages, and in the next panel, the pink-haired protagonist gracefully landed while the unbreakable bear warrior behind her was split in two and collapsed to the ground. The final frame should show Lady Haniel's freeze-frame close-up, yes, yes.
Ah, I'm getting off track, off track! As for the little bear doll left behind after nullification, I asked the old lady at the tailor shop to fix it up. When we defeated the doll, a little wooden horse fell out from the cotton stuffing. That badly beaten Anomaly Hunter said it was his favorite toy as a child, and he couldn't even remember when he lost it. Afterward, both the wooden horse toy and the little bear doll were sent to the Bureau of Anomaly Control for testing. The results showed they weren't Anomalies at all, just ordinary toys. I already returned the little wooden horse to that Anomaly Hunter. I wanted to give him the little bear doll too, but before I could, he ran off faster than when he was getting beaten up.
Hmm… I still can't help but wonder about it. Abandoned toys, a beaten-up Anomaly Hunter… Could it be!? Was that big bear doll a guardian spirit of toys, punishing people who don't cherish their toys? If that's the case, then were we actually the villains in this fairy tale?!
ST_VisionArchives.Hospital_Record_2:
Yeah, I've seen him. It was in a corner of the hospital.
…Anomaly Commission? I don't know about that.
I was in the hospital catching Tamagochi* when I suddenly picked up this weird signal. Some parts were completely static gaps, and others were full of chattering noise. I followed the direction and ran into him, and he noticed me too. There was no hostility in the signal, just more noise, kind of like the snow on old TV screens.
Yeah, he told me about nightmares and the abandoned hospital. I was really interested, so I agreed to his request.
"Go find all the truths."
It was a really amazing process. I just closed my eyes, waited for everything around me to quiet down, and when I opened them, I was already standing in the lobby of that abandoned hospital…
Oh? Are you interested in what's inside too?
Hmm… where do I even start? There are lots of rooms inside, visible ones and invisible ones… and some oddities made of bandages. They were always looking for me and constantly emitting signals full of malice. I felt like they were part of that hospital, including all that malice.
There were some documents, but I didn't pay much attention. I just grabbed them as I went, followed my instincts, and played hide and seek with the oddities along the way.
It's the records room on the second floor. You can get the "truth" he needs there, then leave safely.
Third and fourth floors… I couldn't find a way up, but I could sense some really… strange signals. Not sure what they were.
Yeah, there's definitely more than one.
The specific details and routes… I could tell you, but are you sure you want to hear? Won't you feel spoiled?
Oh, I thought you were asking me all this because you wanted to go there yourself.
Is it scary? I thought it was alright, I actually kind of liked the atmosphere. Maybe because I've seen similar stuff in horror movies… or maybe because I can sense their signals? Whenever they get close, I'm mentally prepared… come to think of it, that's kind of a shame.
Oh right, if you really want to go, here's something only veterans know, and it's my secret to clearing it…
They really can't open cabinets.

*Note: The archivist has confirmed that "Tamagochi" is a concept from the interviewee's virtual pet game and is not an Anomaly or a person's name.

Interesting, isn't it? I also find it very interesting. If this method works, we might be able to nullify an Anomaly by ourselves! I think this is a great opportunity, and our club might even take a revolutionary step…
Uh-oh, the headteacher is coming…! Let's talk about this next time, remember to think about it when you go back! Give me a reply before the holiday!

Before being awakened, the Black Tome was an Object Anomaly resembling a massive book. Its most distinctive feature is the large purple eyeball embedded in its cover, constantly rolling side to side, wary of anyone approaching. Once the Black Tome is opened, the reader will be forcibly dragged into the Anomalous Realm it connects to, known as the "Library," and forced to battle its true form, which is roughly humanoid, with a head resembling an open book, and multiple arm-like appendages coiled around its body. In battle, it summons books inscribed with the beliefs of its followers, from which it fires chains woven from text and flames, or beams of condensed faith energy to devastate its opponents. In addition to these "magical attacks," the Black Tome also possesses a powerful array of physical attacks, capable of manipulating its legs, long tail, or swinging its chains to strike enemies at close range.
The Black Tome draws its power from two main sources: first, by devouring low threat anomalies or nullifying them; second, by controlling low-level anomalies to act in a way that inspires belief in the tome's power, which further amplifies its strength. As the tome's power grows, its Wertheimer Index fluctuates with more intensity. It remains unknown what limit the Black Tome's power could reach if left unchecked.
It must be noted that although the Black Tome absorbs faith from its followers, this process itself is not immediately harmful. Still, its followers may engage in irrational behaviors out of their faith, potentially harming themselves or others. Once the Black Tome is nullified, its followers are freed from their blind faith without lasting effects. However, those who have held the Black Tome for extended periods of time or remained too close may suffer from anomaly encroachment.

When I was little, my grandmother once told me a bedtime story like this.
When she was in school, her class was planning a spring field trip. All her classmates were buzzing with excitement. After all, any activity that meant skipping class is always fun! On the way home, she and a friend who lived nearby chatted about what snacks to bring and what photos they wanted to take. The moment she got home, she could not wait to pack her bag and set three alarms, terrified of oversleeping. But by evening, the sky grew darker and darker. The adults all said that judging by the thickness of the cumulonimbus clouds, the heavy rain would probably last a whole day and night! If it was still raining by the morning, the field trip would be canceled… Grandma climbed into bed, her heart full of worry.
That night, just as expected, the rain began to fall. Lightning lit up her entire room bright as day. She stared glumly out the window for what felt like forever, but the rain showed no sign of letting up. Faced with losing her chance at the field trip, she suddenly remembered the legend of the Rain-sweeping Maid. It was said that this Anomaly could absorb rainwater and make clear skies come sooner. She'd never actually seen one before, but desperately she put her palms together. She faced toward the mop standing in the corner of her room and prayed with all her heart: Rain-sweeping Maid, please help me! Let the weather clear up soon!
Grandma said that even at the time, she felt silly doing it. A mop was just a mop, after all. It was not one of those Anomalies. Even if the Rain-sweeping Maid could somehow hear her wish, could such a small Anomaly actually change the weather? After staring at the mop awkwardly for a while, she was defeated by embarrassment. Too ashamed to look at it any longer, she hurried back under the covers and pulled them over her head, refusing to believe she had really done something so childish.
Before she knew it, she fell asleep… Then, after what could have been any amount of time, a roll of thunder from beyond the horizon jolted her awake. The rain must've gotten even heavier. Disappointed, she crawled out of bed and looked toward the window…
Through the glass, she saw the pouring rain, and countless Rain-sweeping Maid. Raindrops struck their raincoats, making a sound as clear and crisp as silver bells. The rumbling thunder transformed into rhythmic drumbeats, accompanying them. The chiming of countless Rain-sweeping Maid intertwined into a melody, clear, harmonious, and gentle, rippling outward across the night sky.
It was a wondrous… dreamlike scene. Those pure white Anomalies were like little fish, riding the rain that connected heaven and earth, swimming ever upward toward the sky. She did not know where they had come from, whether they had heard her wish, or where they would go afterward. She wasn't even sure if they truly had the power to bring clear skies… but for the rest of that night, Grandma slept soundly, lulled by the gentle song of the Rain-sweeping Maid.
As for whether the next day actually turned out sunny… I fell asleep before hearing the ending, so to this day, I still do not know. But I think the weather might not matter. The miracle on that rainy night must have been far more unforgettable than any ordinary sunny day.

The Resident Association holds free events from time to time, mainly for the elderly and children in the community. The event funds are usually collected in advance, and everyone chips in together. Once we have enough, we throw a little celebration. A friend called me over to help out by dressing up as a mascot to entertain the kids, so I was pretty shocked when I saw someone else dressed as a big bear mascot. I have to say, even though that costume looked a bit worn with some patches on it, the person moved incredibly smoothly! The clanking of the armor sounded so realistic, that outfit must have been really expensive… The kids absolutely loved him. They all crowded around, climbing all over him, and even after the event ended they didn't want him to leave. Nobody even wanted the frog balloons I was handing out nearby. But after the event, when I went to return my costume to the volunteers, I asked them how they managed to splurge on such a nice bear costume this time. They told me: "Bear mascot? There wasn't one. We only hired you."
…It must have been some kind-hearted person who didn't want to reveal their identity. Oh well, as long as the kids were happy, that's all that matters.

ST_VisionArchives.BObⅡM-3412_VisionDesc:
An Object Anomaly resembling a discarded roll of film, surrounded by scattered floating photos, with common darkroom language like "Keep The Room Dark" in the center. It shows no clear intent to attack but prefers to lock onto targets with a camera's viewfinder, stealthily recording and capturing them. With each shutter click, the captured target may vanish, turn into a photograph, or be cast into the Negative Space. In the Negative Space, the fragmented film entity can launch physical attacks or attack with previously recorded images.
The first instance of Film - MANISH appeared at the Film Orbit Studio in Bridge Crossings, only to be nullified by the Anomaly Hunter organization, Eibon Antique Shop. Manish hailed from Lux Imaging Company's esteemed lineup. The celebrated company was famed for its photographic films, chemicals, cameras, and related gear. The advent of new photography technologies nudged traditional films out of the limelight, plummeting MANISH sales and leading to its eventual phase-out. This decline is believed to have sparked the anomalization of Film - MANISH.

ST_VisionArchives.SchoolMyth_RecordBefore_2:
I never imagined that the sketch mannequin abandoned in the art room would become my partner.
Its name is Click-Clack, it's a broken model.  Its left leg joint is loose and its right index finger is missing a piece. Anyway, last Friday night, when I was alone in the classroom practicing sketches, it started moving before my eyes.
I quickly covered my artwork and apologized to Click-Clack—it looked so much better than what I had drawn. But Click-Clack was grateful to me, pointing at the drawing with its broken finger. That's when I realized that despite my clumsy drawing skills, I had used my imagination to complete Click-Clack's palm.
Sketching pursues realism, and everyone would focus on depicting Click-Clack's flaws, but… I had accidentally smoothed over its scars…
What happened next felt like a dream. Even when I roughly sketched an outline, Click-Clack would pose exactly the same way the next day. My classmates all envied my hyperrealistic drawing skills, but only I knew that the mannequin in the corner was subtly adjusting its shoulder angle—making it match the height in my drawing.
'You're a natural! Those eyes are like a camera!' The art teacher's excited voice echoed through the hallway. Under her praise, the principal approached me and asked me to paint portraits of all the school teachers to update the faculty wall.
After forcing myself to finish the paintings, my heart felt like stagnant water.
I realized I was nothing without Click-Clack… This thought drove me to pick the art room lock at dawn. The mannequin stood quietly in the moonlight. I tremblingly touched its palm, begging Click-Clack to help me one more time. It had no expression, but somehow you could sense it was deep in thought on that blank face.
Then its neck stiffly nodded with a click-clack sound.
But… it seemed to misunderstand what I meant.
I wanted the mannequin to help me cheat! Sneak into each teacher's house under cover of night, punch the math teacher's face crooked to make it look just how I'd drawn it asymmetrically, cut the principal's hair into a receding hairline since I'd forgotten to draw it, tattoo the PE teacher with the Ora Puncher tattoo I accidentally added… In short, if I could make the real world match my paintings, I'd be a genius forever!
But Click-Clack, it turned Room 105 into an infinitely extending white cage, then kept changing poses in front of the easel, telling me I could only leave by drawing correctly… At first I thought it was joking, but when I discovered that no matter how I turned the door handle, Room 105 was always behind me… I realized it was serious.
Drawing papers soon reached my ankles. Every time I was about to finish, that damn joint would click-clack again, cheating by changing its pose. This would be futile—I'd never be able to draw Click-Clack exactly the same!
Until one dawn, I collapsed and knocked over the easel. Click-Clack suddenly froze, pointing with its broken finger at the drawings scattered on the floor—on those papers I had considered failed drafts, from the initial stiff lines to the final works that almost seemed to leap off the page, techniques and talent I never had before had already been remembered by my brush through this period of grueling practice.
Moonlight streamed through the mannequin's loose joints, casting star-like spots on the floor. I finally understood that this art room had never been locked, but rather… it was through my struggle with myself that I truly found the strength to push open the door.
ST_VisionArchives.OceanChase_RecordBefore_1:
I heard on Bagel that if you drive through the undersea tunnel and suddenly hear whale calls out of nowhere, you might enter some kind of special Anomalous Realm. It was getting tons of discussion online. As an Anomaly exploration blogger, I thought to myself, of course I can't pass up this opportunity for views.
…No, no, no, I didn't actually want to go there. I didn't even believe it at first. I just planned to drive through the undersea tunnel, shoot some footage, add whale sounds in post, put on a dramatic performance, and rake in some views. Who could have known…
Honestly, if you hadn't come to interview me, I wouldn't even want to remember what happened that day.
That day, I set up my cameras on the roof and the inside of my car like usual, drove through the undersea tunnel for a bit, and started recording. Then suddenly, I heard whale calls… The sound was so strange and beautiful, it completely captured all my attention…
When I snapped back to reality, I found myself surrounded by darkness. There was only a faint path visible ahead of me, and the whale calls in my ears were getting closer and closer… I totally panicked and could only speed up, driving forward.
Then this… whale-like monster flew right over my head, and this blinding light made it impossible to open my eyes. I was so terrified I hit the gas instead of the brake and crashed right in…
Damn it, let me think about how to put this… I crashed into this nightmare of a place. There was rain falling from the sky, ice covering the ground, broken buildings floating in midair, and these massive ship anchors taller than buildings stuck in a blood-red sea like tombstones… That whale was wailing in the red sea, and I could feel it watching me. I thought I was going to die and just passed out from hyperventilating…
After that… I don't remember. When I woke up, I was back in the undersea tunnel. My cameras were damaged and didn't capture anything.
But… you have to believe me, it was absolutely real! My tires still had ice chunks on them afterward! That definitely wasn't just a nightmare…
ST_VisionArchives.BuildingDrawing_Record_1:
I'm the guy from that construction site. We'd already clocked out for the day and were planning to grab a few drinks, but halfway through my first beer, I realized I'd left my tools on the rooftop. I remembered the weather report said it would rain that night, and I'd even covered all the machines and materials with tarps before leaving, but somehow I forgot about the tools! If those things got soaked, it would've been a disaster… No, no, not a safety issue or anything. Broken tools can be replaced with new ones, but they'd dock my pay! Isn't that awful?!
I shot up at the thought of losing money and headed back to the site. Before I even got upstairs, I heard rustling sounds coming from inside the building. It was late at night, the safety inspector had gone home, my coworkers were out drinking, and the security guard had just been dozing at the gate… So who could it be? Come on, take a guess!
Ha! How was I supposed to know it was an Anomaly back then! Of course I thought it was a thief! Back when I was younger, I'd seen plenty of crooks sneaking onto sites to steal metal… What? I never did that myself! You better write that down clearly! Don't let this Commission get out there and cost me my job!
Ahem… seriously though, I was pretty scared, so I grabbed a water pipe and carefully crept closer… turns out it was this huge… newspaper… or whatever it was? I was still wondering what the heck it was, when… WOOSH! It spun around and wrapped me up!
Next thing I knew, whoa! Like something out of a dream, all the buildings around me had turned black and white. There was this big building in the middle… looked like the one we were working on, but not quite right? The facade had all these messy illegal structures sticking out, just floating there in mid-air. If the safety inspector saw that, he'd probably faint…
Climb? Are you kidding me! That structure looked completely unstable! Besides, I remembered what the guys had been talking about while drinking. There's this legend about an Anomaly on the construction site that drags people into its lair, and if you just stay there and don't do anything for a while, you can get out. So I just wandered around for a bit, and sure enough, I got out… But what I didn't expect was that when I came out of the Anomalous Realm, it was already pouring rain outside…
No, they didn't dock my pay after all. Since I got caught by an Anomaly, according to regulations I wasn't liable for damages. But I still got a good scolding… haaah…
ST_VisionArchives.PObⅡS-1113_RecordBefore2:
I've called the hotline many times. What is even being built here? Will it ever be finished?
Morning? Drilling and thumping in MORNING? Isn't the morning for sleeping? Evening? Even less so. When it gets dark, stop working. Daylight saving time was invented for a reason! Don't work on rainy days either, it's all muddy around here, and on sunny days, the dust flies everywhere, it's unbearable.
So, I ask, will it ever be finished? It's not like I'm protesting against the entire project, but don't get me started with that blade stuck in the dirt now. Did some cosplayer got into the site and halted all your progress? Get your arses together, work day, work night, work rainy, work sunny, work whatever, I honestly don't care, but get it done. It's affecting housing prices 'round here.
ST_VisionArchives.NiKanDao_Record_1:
I discovered this painting while on a trip to Miguel District. A strange wooden figure was pointing at it, but I couldn't understand what that meant. Plus, the wooden figure looked kind of creepy… so I quickly walked away. But after walking off, I couldn't help wanting to turn back and see what was inside the painting. The moment I turned around, I noticed that the door in the painting lined up perfectly with the door frame behind the canvas.
"That's pretty interesting," I thought, and in that instant, I was transported into the Anomalous Realm. This wasn't my first time entering an Anomalous Realm, so I wasn't that scared.
The puzzles inside were simple enough, just matters of perspective. I was able to quickly find the exit.
Before leaving, I turned around one more time. Though these rooms looked bizarre, they also felt cozy, and the longer I stayed, the more beautiful they seemed. A sudden thought occurred to me: could I just stay here forever?

Another thought pushed it aside: I have school tomorrow, and an exam the day after.
After escaping, the whole experience felt like I had just spaced out for a moment. It was so light and fleeting that even the clouds in the sky hadn't moved much.
What would happen if I really did stay inside forever?
ST_VisionArchives.Anomaly0118_RecordBefore1:
I once encountered it while on night duty, pursuing other Anomalies. The section was under lockdown for containment purposes, and to swiftly contain the Anomaly, I used the long-practiced "Z Drift" to ensure its capture! However, the dashboard suddenly displayed inexplicable gibberish, which I initially attributed to late-night fatigue… until a motorcycle Anomaly with blue flames appeared on the road, speeding away. Even though my beloved car had modifications to the spoiler, engine, and suspension system, it couldn't keep up. That night, I thought I had met the king of racers…

Ultimately, I fell into an anomalous space, its enormous scythe and roaring motorcycle left me a deep impression. The ending wasn't pleasant, as the Anomaly executed dazzling motorcycle combo moves that couldn't be overcome despite my best efforts. However, since then, I haven't driven over the speed limit, which is a blessing in disguise.
ST_VisionArchives.PObⅡS-5701_RecordBefore:
I once encountered that type of special entity after a night shift on the street.
Because I have a similar Ora Puncher at home, which I use as a massage tool, I naturally thought someone lost theirs and was considering taking it to lost and found. But then railings and warning lights suddenly appeared around me, and a ring rose up under my feet, lifting me up…
I realized something was wrong and quickly climbed out of the ring, distancing myself from the puncher. When I looked back, the ring had disappeared, and the puncher lay quietly on the ground…
If the Ora Punchers' abilities hadn't been confirmed, I'd have thought I was seeing things from exhaustion…
ST_VisionArchives.NiKanDao_Record_3:
I've seen this painting and entered that strange space. It uses puzzles to convey its concepts. A very unique Anomaly.
Vision doesn't reflect the world, it retells it. Light that has been reprocessed through neural transmission is no longer the same beam of light. Our vision is just another canvas, and our brain repaints using the pigments received by our eyes. Colors are refractions of light, forms are reconstructions by the brain. We can never truly see real reality, and precisely because of this, we're born with the ability to seek reality on canvas.
This Anomaly tells us through its fragmented assemblage how fascinating the construction of illusion can be. Scenes in dreams always combine in bizarre and fantastic ways, and within the Anomaly, we can achieve this process while awake. Anything that can be visually connected can be combined together. This method of combination breaks free from the constraints of an object's essence, allowing them to envision new possibilities through pure imagery. The world in an artist's eyes is free.
By the way, I heard this artist has quite a few surviving works? Can anyone help me get in touch with acquisition channels? I'd really love to collect one. Name your price!
ST_VisionArchives.Boss33_VisionDescBefore:
A giant, mask-wearing avian Anomaly that lures lost children to its nest. It tempts abducted children into calling it "Mommy." Once successful, the children lose their sense of self, forget their past, and come to sincerely regard the Nestbound Bird as their mother.
However, the Nestbound Bird does nothing to nurture or care for these children. It simply keeps them trapped in its nest. To possess children means to be a mother. It revels in nothing more than this self-satisfaction.
ST_VisionArchives.Boss33_VisionDescAfter:

ST_VisionArchives.RainLiyuuQi_VisionDescBefore:
Obsessed with finding and crossing the Dragon Gate, the carp continuously descend from the heavens to this place, only to return to the sky after failing. But this endless migration is not without merit—when carp that have experienced multiple failed journeys descend from the heavens once more, the storms they bring are proof of their constant transformation. For the people living here, the winds and rains that accompany this migration are nothing if not a potential calamity.
Of course, despite their continuous transformation, their pursuit of the Dragon Gate remains unchanged, and they will still actively challenge anything that might possibly be the Dragon Gate…
Carp at this stage have an even stronger desire to challenge. Once someone rides upon them, they will carry that person to where their companions are located, and regardless of whether the challenge succeeds or fails, the carp will swim back to the sky and disappear.

ST_VisionArchives.Hospital_VisionDescBefore:
According to the client, this Anomaly's main body is an abandoned medical facility called ██ Hospital. Its geographical location has not been confirmed. The client describes it as "located deep within nightmares," and investigators must accept hypnosis and guidance to enter the described "dreamscape" to observe the facility. According to the client's explanation, after accepting hypnosis, investigators will enter a state of deep sleep lasting anywhere from thirty minutes to several days, potentially accompanied by adverse reactions including sleep talking, body tremors, unconscious scratching, and rapid breathing. However, these reactions all disappear once the hypnosis ends and the investigator awakens. The client refuses to reveal the principles behind entering this area.
As of now, there is no visual documentation of this Anomaly's internal structure, and related investigation records are extremely limited. Among interviewees claiming to have undergone hypnosis, over half indicate the client likely suffers from mental disorders or is suspected of fraud. A minority of interviewees confirm having entered a facility called ██ Hospital under hypnosis and observing "Anomalies composed of bandages" within. Beyond this, different interviewees' accounts vary significantly.
Supplementary record: Historical profiles contain no queries for any real medical institution named ██ Hospital. It does not exist.

So keep your eyes peeled and stay sharp in there!

ST_VisionArchives.ElevatorAnomaly_01_VisionDescBefore:
If left alone long enough, this situation will naturally resolve itself. Level Proliferation is less of an Object Anomaly that transforms from a normal elevator, and more of a malfunction phenomenon that can randomly occur in otherwise normal elevators.
This phenomenon causes the elevator to go haywire, unable to reach its original floors, with a high probability of connecting to random Anomalous Realms. The stairs in the same building remain completely unaffected.
As long as everyone in the building commits to taking the stairs instead of the elevator for one year, the Anomaly will undergo natural Nullification. Simple enough… However, the reality is that residents (except those on the second floor) always pool their funds at the first opportunity and post high-paying emergency commissions to the Guild.
ST_VisionArchives.ElevatorAnomaly_01_VisionDescAfter:

ST_VisionArchives.Boss08_VisionDescBefore:
Swallowtail was first sighted near a school. It takes the form of a giant butterfly with vivid coloring. Its body is composed of numerous paper scraps resembling movie ticket stubs, making it only capable of low altitude flight. However, Swallowtail seems to constantly attempt flying higher in vain.
There are many theories regarding Swallowtail's origin. The most widely circulated source is an urban legend about a girl named Butterfly who collected countless movie ticket stubs, lost herself in the fantasy of film, and eventually vanished without a trace.
The legend is incomplete, but one thing is certain: the birth of Swallowtail stems from her actions.
ST_VisionArchives.Boss08_VisionDescAfter:
Swallowtail was first sighted near a school. It takes the form of a giant butterfly with vivid coloring. Its body is composed of numerous paper scraps resembling movie ticket stubs, making it only capable of low altitude flight. However, Swallowtail seems to constantly attempt flying higher in vain.
There are many theories regarding Swallowtail's origin. The most widely circulated source is an urban legend about a girl named Butterfly who collected countless movie ticket stubs, lost herself in the fantasy of film, and eventually vanished without a trace.
The legend is incomplete, but one thing is certain: the birth of Swallowtail stems from her actions.
Swallowtail exhibits extreme aggression toward humans. Multiple witnesses claim to have seen Swallowtail kill passersby. However, no casualties have ever occurred at sighting locations, suggesting that Swallowtail possesses the ability to create illusions.
In fact, Swallowtail only inflicts actual harm on those who attack it. Several Anomaly Hunters who attempted Nullification have been attacked, with some sustaining life-threatening injuries.

ST_VisionArchives.RainLiyuuQi_RecordBefore_2:
People have long suspected that challenging the Dragon Gate, even when unsuccessful, would strengthen the Skyfish Banner participating in Tidal Ascension, and the appearance of Tides of Misfortune has confirmed this theory… While the weather changes brought by Tides of Misfortune can only affect a small area, we still cannot ignore the potential harm it might cause. Fortunately, its behavioral patterns haven't changed much compared to Tidal Ascension…
It's important to note that since reaching Tides of Misfortune requires riding the Skyfish Banner, and Tides of Misfortune often appears on rooftops higher than Tidal Ascension, groups attempting Nullification together must be very careful, as the Skyfish Banner only provides limited footing.
Also, if you have contracted Oddities that aren't very obedient, it's best not to make them your target…
ST_VisionArchives.Anomaly0163_RecordBeforeContent_2:
Recently, the biggest stir caused by Doomscroll was when it was mistakenly displayed on a large outdoor billboard, making everyone passing by stop and stare, right?
I was actually there that day with my best friend, shopping, and we happened to see it. We saw a crowd gathered and thought it was a celebrity meet-and-greet, so we went closer to check it out. That was a mistake. Just a few glances and she was entranced, refusing to move, whispering "just a little longer, just a little longer". The result was that she seemed rooted to the spot like a tree! No matter what I said or did to remind her that our movie was starting, it was useless! Other than the Anomaly Video on the big screen, she couldn't see, hear, or focus on anything else. Fortunately, the video's control over her was almost over, so my "zombie" friend and I didn't have to wait too long.
Why wasn't I affected? Check out these glasses thicker than a bottle bottom! Got it?
ST_VisionArchives.SchoolMyth_RecordBefore_1:
Strange incidents have been popping up all over school lately, leaving everyone on edge. As a member of the Mystery Club, I've uncovered the patterns behind these events and compiled them into my notes: "Six Unreliable Theories About Campus Supernatural Phenomena". Limited budget means no printing—please share this manually.
(Warning: Do not circulate these observation notes within the dean's line of sight)

"Forever 105"—this has to be the dean's handiwork! A "Remedial Self-Discipline Classroom!" Specifically designed to punish students who love copying homework. Those being punished must rewrite the same problem over and over until they produce an original answer. To escape Room 105… you'll have to use your brain, literally…
"Mysterious Thumping in Late-Night Hallways"—don't worry, it's the PE teacher's secret training! Those invisible impacts are meant to train students' reflexes. If you can stay standing after being hit by something invisible, you'll master the basics of dodgeball.
"Cup Guessing Game in the Baking Classroom"—just girls doing love divination. Among three upside-down shaking cups, guess which one has your crush's name written on the bottom… but from what I know, you'll never guess right! The person guessing will always deny it! Well, that's what youth is all about. Right or wrong doesn't matter—what's important is the guesser's reaction. Often their eyes are still looking away while their breathing has already betrayed them like a drum. The cups gently tap, questioning heartbeats, and a girl's blush speaks louder than words.
In the music room, there seems to be a "Piano That Loves Entertaining Itself"—when no one's playing, it performs solo concerts at midnight. Its specialty is "Mathematical Dance in G Major," a piece so intricate and complex that listening to it really feels like attending a math class. When it gets tired… it even plays lullabies in the lower register to put itself to sleep. What a selfish piano that only cares about its own fun and not others' well-being! Worth learning from for students with fragile hearts.
On the playground, there's a "Teleporting Cheater Doll"—this is some track team senior's obsession! They were always getting overtaken during races, and even frantically practiced techniques to avoiding false starts. Over time, their strong desire to win gave birth to this doll. Now whenever the referee looks down, it instantly vanishes, having perfected its craft.
There are also two mysterious "Magician Dolls"—one specializes in "Invisibility and Escape," the other in "Making People Float Then Teleport." There must be an epic story behind this! For instance, they're cursed symbiotes who were once a pair of close human brothers. The illegitimate older brother was always the invisible one in the family. His presence erased, forbidden from appearing in public view for life. The younger brother was an heir yearning for freedom, but the curse made it impossible for him to escape control. This bred a strong desire to flee, freezing people at a safe distance, refusing anyone's approach…
The two magician dolls can only break the curse by touching each other, but their abilities are designed so that they can never get close to one another. This is fate's mockery—playful yet full of malice.

Conclusion: Anyway… while these weird phenomena aren't deadly, they'll trap you in endless trouble. With finals approaching, getting caught up in this and missing exams would be disaster. Everyone please be careful! After all… you wouldn't want to be locked in the looping Room 105 for remedial study, would you?
ST_VisionArchives.PPhⅠS-13_RecordBefore:
Man, the deliveries are non-stop lately. Got sidetracked by a rush order and nearly lost a package. Would've cost me! Finally found it in the warehouse, unwrapped… Just as I breathed a sigh of relief, I opened the door to find a cardboard box city! The more I walked, the more boxes there were, and they almost formed a wall! I was baffled: where did all these packages come from?
Oh, you have no idea how scary it is to walk among a pile of stacked cardboard boxes. It felt as if they could collapse any second! Luckily, after sealing the package, the boxes disappeared, and the items inside were fine. Otherwise, this month's work would have been for nothing! Thinking back, it felt like a maze… If I run into that mess again, I'm switching to food delivery, no joke!
ST_VisionArchives.ElevatorAnomaly_01_Record_3:
Does anyone else feel an inexplicable sense of awe toward elevators?
I'm not talking about getting motion sick in elevators, nor psychological trauma from being trapped in one.
I don't feel this way about cars or planes. Even in enclosed vehicles, I can still perceive the outside world through windows. Elevators… are different.
Maybe it's because I've always had an overactive imagination, and with Anomalies existing in our world, I can't help but wonder… When the elevator doors open, isn't it like opening a Mystery Box to an unknown world?
Oh, though technically the elevator car itself is the smaller box.

For example, I've imagined the elevator doors opening to find:
A precision strike laser has reduced my home and all my belongings to rubble.
A flood rushes in and sweeps me away, and when I open my eyes, I seamlessly transition into a deserted island survival situation.
My zombified parents lunging at my face with their gaping, bloody maws.
I step out into a perfectly normal-looking scene, unaware it's actually a vacuum, and I'm crushed or torn apart in the sensation of weightlessness, only to open my eyes again as some white-haired old man covered in scientific instruments tells me, "The experiment is over."
…Of course, there's also the possibility of a bright-eyed pretty girl standing outside with an enthusiastic smile, congratulating me on being reincarnated into a fantasy world, where I'll start from Lvl 1 with the worst possible skills and work my way up to becoming the hero who saves the world.

None of these delusions have ever come true, but my sense of awe toward elevators hasn't diminished one bit even after using them so often.
Riding an elevator alone is probably the most frequent opportunity in daily life to temporarily isolate oneself from the rest of the world… In those tiny, fleeting yet extremely frequent fragments of time, I'm placed in a Mystery Box. The outside world too is placed in a Mystery Box, and I can't prove it remains as it was, and it loses me. When I think about it that way, it actually feels pretty nice.
Ah, especially when there's absolutely no signal in this elevator and I can't even post on Bagel, these delusions become incredibly immersive.
Like right now. I'm alone here, the elevator doors seem to be inexplicably stuck, there's enough oxygen at least, but pressing the call button for ages hasn't gotten any response. So, I'm bored enough to write this rambling essay on my phone… though normally, a single elevator ride would never be long enough to write this much. Since I've written so much, I'll just post it once I get signals again.
By the way, there's an "Emergency Start" button here. Maybe it could open the elevator doors? I've never pressed a button like this before, and without internet, I can't look up whether it's safe to use in this situation…
The sense of presence is incredible. This is the most nervous I've ever been.

…

Addendum:
This manuscript was discovered in the drafts folder of the Bagel app on a phone recovered from the elevator car at the scene.
No bloodstains or signs of struggle were found inside the car. Blurry footage from the elevator's security camera shows the subject pausing in surprise when the elevator doors opened, then cautiously stepping outside. They returned to the elevator approximately fifteen minutes later, deliberately left their phone behind, waved toward the camera, and stepped outside the elevator once more.
The subject's current whereabouts are unknown after the Level Proliferation Anomaly manifested in the elevator they were riding. It is presumed they became lost in one of the floors of the Anomalous Realm…
ST_VisionArchives.NiKanDao_Record_2:
The wooden lady invited me to see the door to her home, then brought me inside as a guest. Her house was huge, with three rooms that had suns, moons, and bones hanging in them. Doors were hidden in shadows, shadows were hidden in light, and light was hidden in eyes. I walked between the sun and moon as they silently invited me to watch them embrace and devour each other.

Our shadows followed behind us, but the shadows weren't us. They danced hand in hand, with books and bones beneath their feet. I moved through the gaps between walls and beams of light just like they did. In my eyes, the massive and the tiny made no difference. The light flattened everything, and my eyes flattened everything I saw too. Then the flattened things overlapped with other flattened things to create a new painting. In that painting, I was free. I stepped onto the flattened stairs and said goodbye to the wooden lady.

…What's wrong? Why are you looking at me like that?

…Do these things sound strange? This is what happened to me yesterday.

Do you want to go see it? If you want to go, I can take you there!
ST_VisionArchives.PObⅠS-7605_RecordBefore2:
Here are my exclusive tips on how to quickly find the Nexus in the Spacetime Projector:
1. Record the Video duration.
2. Watch 13 more times and note any inconsistencies. (PS: 13 is my lucky number)
3. Conduct a thorough search of the sections with the recorded inconsistencies.
4. If nothing is found, use frame-by-frame playback to continue the investigation.
5. Prepare food and water before entering the Video.
I hold the record for the longest case-solving time in the Video at 19 hours, which remains unbeaten. Hope my tips are helpful to you all!

ST_VisionArchives.C-7111Ob_RecordBeforeContent_1:
More than the Black Tome itself, I think the people who exploit this kind of anomalies are far worse! I've been through many cases like this. Someone claimed that "if you follow the Black Tome's teachings, you can master magic" and "magic is a power that belongs to everyone and is greater than Esper Abilities." They used that whole spiel to trick so many people!
…Hm? How did I figure out he was a scammer? Ahaha… this is a bit embarrassing… Do I really have to tell you?
Well… several "magical incantations" printed in the Black Tome, the ones that guy claimed were real spells, were random words I wrote back in middle school… I'm guessing the other "incantations" were probably just made up by fellow online emo kids. I have no idea where they dug up all those phrases. It wasn't from Bagel, was it? I already set all my Bagel posts from before high school to private… Wait, is the "Black" in "Black Tome" actually short for "Black Hat Hacker"? Can it pull up archived web pages or something?
Urgh, I'm getting off track. Anyway, I heard later that the guy who used the Black Tome to trick people was just someone who desperately wanted to feel special, and that's how the Black Tome got to him… If that's true, he's kind of pitiful in a way. B-but of course, I'm not defending him or anything! No matter how special you want to be, it's still wrong to trick people! What if someone actually believed him and thought they'd learn real magic, then hurt themselves trying to cast those so-called "spells"? I just… somewhat get how he feels, that's it… wanting to be special. Hoping you won't just live an unremarkable life.
But thinking about it, aren't we all already special in our own way? Even without Esper Abilities, magic, or any extraordinary powers, there will never be another Haniel in this world! And if there really were another me who was exactly the same… don't you think that itself sounds like the beginning of an epic story? "The ordinary girl Haniel one day encounters a girl with the same looks, voice, personality, hobbies… Is she a twin sister separated at birth? Or a clone created by some mysterious organization? Or perhaps 'Haniel' is actually the model name of a mass-produced robot, and she, unaware of this fact, has always believed herself to be human…?" The more I think about it, the more interesting it gets! Yep, that's what I'll daydream about before bed tonight!
ST_VisionArchives.PObⅡS-39_RecordBefore2:
Security Office Case Record: Tear Gas Package Incident
Record Content:
At 5:47 AM, the Security Office received a report call from citizen Josh. According to Josh's description in the call, while jogging in the morning, he passed an alley and heard someone calling for help. Upon approaching, he first smelled a pungent chili odor, and then his eyes felt intense pain and he couldn't stop tearing up. It is suspected that he encountered tear gas.
Officers arrived at the scene five (5) minutes later and met the reporter Josh. The tear gas leak was outdoors. The gas had dissipated, and Josh was unharmed. Officers searched the vicinity and quickly found another injured person, along with scattered broken plastic bottles. The injured person, wearing a courier uniform, was found with eyes tightly shut and coughing uncontrollably. After being transferred to the hospital, the next day, the courier, Trent went to the Security Office for a case record.
According to Trent, he received an urgent order that early morning, requiring a package to be delivered to the square by 06:00 sharp. When picking up the goods, Trent didn't see the sender, and the payment was completed online in advance. Although finding it odd, Trent didn't think much of it. While passing through a small alley on the east side of the square, Trent described being tripped by something. The package contained fragile items, so Trent immediately went to inspect it, not noticing the colorful graffiti on the wall moving. Arms extended from the wall and snatched the package away.
Trent sensed he might have encountered an Anomaly and wanted to retrieve the package and escape. During the struggle, the colorful graffiti goof emerged from the wall.
According to Trent's, the package was shaken violently and emitted a faint hissing sound. The creature threw the package into the air, and it suddenly exploded, while the creature rode off on a skateboard. Amid the strong pungent smell, Trent soon couldn't open his eyes and could only call for help.
The timing of Trent's distress call matches the description from the reporter Josh.
The follow-up will focus on investigating the package sender. Homemade tear gas is a serious offense against Hethereau laws; and if the package had successfully reached the densely populated square center, it could have caused more serious consequences.
Record Note:
Colorful Graffiti Monster; humanoid, tall; body composed of bright colors, similar to wall spray paints; uses a skateboard. (BAC informed)

ST_VisionArchives.PPhⅠS-13_RecordBefore_2:
In theory, as long as you don't try to close it, Proliferative C won't harm people. It doesn't actively attack humans, nor will it collapse due to external influences, even if you crash directly into the walls formed by the cardboard boxes. Though, I still want to warn all Anomaly Hunters here: don't let your guard down just because Proliferative C won't actively harm people! Proliferative C spawns new boxes based on human behavior, which means your next step might be completely clear, or you might crash straight into a wall. Therefore, slow down and watch where you're going.
By the way, although Proliferative C looks like cardboard boxes, they're actually extremely hard. If you crash into them… you might want to look into the price of getting a new alloy nose bridge…

ST_VisionArchives.OceanChase_CusConmment_2_Dis_Player:

Its purpose in singing whale songs and guiding humans into the passages of the Anomalous Realm was perhaps to hope that someone might understand the meaning of this prison and bring an end to its endless torment.
May there come a day when all life treats one another with kindness.

ST_VisionArchives.OceanChase_CusConmment_1_Dis_Player:
A Bio Anomaly born from a whale attacked by a whaling vessel, with a harpoon still lodged in its back, where flesh and metal have fused into one. This anomaly has long been trapped within an Anomalous Realm of glaciers and seas of blood. The harpoon itself is a type of anomaly, and the agony it brings is precisely what causes the whale to lose control within the Anomalous Realm. Regrettably, since the harpoon has fused with the whale's vital organs, it would be impossible to remove without killing the whale.
Nullification has been confirmed. No more seas of blood, no more whale songs.
ST_VisionArchives.RainLiyuuQi_RecordBefore_3: The storms brought by the current carp are hardly what you'd call a disaster, but what we really need to guard against is whatever appears after they cross the Dragon Gate. The records are too ancient and the Yggash Court's archives contain only scattered rumors of Him, but after that great catastrophe… In any case, since Tides of Misfortune have appeared, perhaps His arrival isn't far off either. We ask everyone to pay close attention to "Tidal Ascension" and its derivative Anomalies, take your trials with them seriously, and report any new intel gathered during the process to the Yggash Court.
ST_VisionArchives.PObⅢS-1348_RecordBefore1:
See an unattended umbrella on the street and think about turning it in to the lost and found? 
Let me remind everyone to stay alert! Don't rush—keep a safe distance and take a closer look. Is there a black, muddy puddle underneath it? Are there any suspicious, tentacle-like objects dangling from the umbrella? If the answer is yes, I urge all citizens to leave the area immediately and contact the JTF. Let the professionals handle it. What looks like an umbrella is actually the Anomaly known as the Rainman in its dormant state. Approaching it recklessly could have serious consequences.
ST_VisionArchives.PObⅢS-1348_RecordAfter:
I really wish they'd make a new regulation: No graffiti artists allowed to draw potentially misleading art on Hethereau's streets!
You know what they say? Behind every ridiculous rule is an even more ridiculous lesson learned…
Just who—deliberately—drew such a realistic water puddle on the ground—and even topped it off with a black umbrella?!
At that moment… Filled with excitement thinking "Gotcha!", I rolled up my sleeves and got ready to pounce on the Rainman in front of me with my most agile and confident stance, planning to end this quickly!
Instead, I face-planted right into the ground, nearly bit my tongue, and ended up with this umbrella on my head that looked just like a Rainman's but was absolutely, positively fake! And now my uniform is covered in this sticky, pitch-black spray paint that was used to draw those fake water stains!!!
Who in the world did this?!

ST_VisionArchives.Anomaly0030_RecordBeforeContent_3:
These Anomalies aren't usually troublesome—just a quick cleanup. But when we get these commissions, everyone tries to pass them off until we draw lots.
You probably know that the Anomalous Realms they create are like warped theme parks of the stolen inspiration. One step in there and you'll know exactly what was going on in the victim's head.
It's not as fun as it sounds. I once helped my favorite manga artist and got the ultimate spoiler for her series' ending. All the anticipation and excitement, gone in an instant. I was looking forward to celebrating the final chapter with my friends and savoring the story's end…
Sorry, got carried away there. These realms can be more complex than others. If the inspiration's owner is a horror director, you're in for an unforgettable nightmare. A colleague nearly got lost in a mystery novelist's realm and was freaking out. Would that count as a workplace injury?
We also have to sign NDAs and contracts, which is a pain. The commission fee isn't high, but the regulations are endless. No wonder nobody wants these jobs…
ST_VisionArchives.Anomaly0030_AnniCondAfter: A flyswatter or insecticide might be needed. Pursuing into the Anomalous Realm when necessary.
ST_VisionArchives.PObⅢS-1348_RecordBefore2:
We've all seen Rainmen disguised as umbrellas on the streets. But what happens on rainy nights? Do they immediately transform into their recognizable forms?
II'm sure many Anomaly Hunters share this curiosity, but I might be the only one daring enough to investigate firsthand. The result, however, might disappoint you: Nothing happened! That imagined scene of thin, elongated tentacles twisting and stretching from the umbrella to form a suited office worker shakily standing up—it never occurred! Was it simply not planning to join its companions in the hunt?
After consulting an expert in Anomaly research, they provided this explanation: It makes sense if we view their stationary behavior as standing guard. Normally, we're dragged into Rainman territory when we get too close, right? Perhaps their appearance marks the connection point between their world and ours. They might stay rooted as beacons for their companions to find their way home, standing firm until the rainy night passes.
So, in a way, they're actually quite loyal to one another, aren't they?
ST_VisionArchives.Sadbear_VisionDescBefore: Abandoned dolls that remain untreated for extended periods may transform into large, tattered plush toys wearing cloaks and wielding weapons. They typically appear in secluded areas of parks, playgrounds, and other locations frequented by children. Anyone who enters its territory will become trapped within Saddy Teddy's fairy tale, with defeating it being the only way to escape.
ST_VisionArchives.Sadbear_VisionDescAfter:

ST_VisionArchives.PaperCastle_VisionDescAfter:
Before activation, this Anomaly appears as a massive golden wax seal, typically resting stationary on flat street surfaces. Any human who accidentally makes direct contact with the wax imprint will be transported into a pop-up book style Anomalous Realm and attacked by its core entity, the Cardboard Castle. This appears to be some form of overly forceful invitation, and it's clear that the Expired Invitation has no understanding of proper hospitality.
The Cardboard Castle employs spring-loaded streamers, red carpets, and cardboard weapons to launch simultaneous attacks from multiple angles. While it appears similar to ordinary corrugated cardboard, its hardness, elasticity, and unit weight far exceed normal paper products, making its destructive power considerable.
Though the Cardboard Castle possesses significant attack power, its mobility is inversely proportional to its strength. Maintaining sufficient distance from the Cardboard Castle allows one to escape the Anomalous Realm independently. Once the target flees, the Anomalous Realm will temporarily close and revert to its harmless golden wax seal form, awaiting the next innocent passerby.
Given that its duration is indefinite, waiting for natural Nullification is not advisable. Capable Anomaly Hunters can completely nullify the Expired Invitation by thoroughly tearing apart the Cardboard Castle. After Nullification, the wax seal will burn itself out completely, leaving behind a treasure chest at the original location.
The origin of this treasure chest remains unclear in current research. One mainstream and imaginative hypothesis suggests it may have been the "party favor" originally prepared for the "banquet" guests.

ST_VisionArchives.Boombox_VisionDescBefore:
This Object Anomaly consists of a set of electronic music production and performance equipment. These devices can operate without power and combine into specific formations that move autonomously, appearing and active in the Clement Music Corner.
The Beat King can be dormant or activated. When dormant, it appears as equipment scattered across the plaza. When activated, the Anomaly hovers and moves autonomously, challenging people in the plaza.
When a challenge begins, the Beat King plays electronic music and creates glowing projections in the plaza that indicate volume levels. The reason for its challenging behavior remains unknown, but it's confirmed that the Anomaly attacks following the rhythm of its music, forcing challengers to make actions that match the beat. If challengers make mistakes, they suffer intense sound wave attacks that can cause unconsciousness in severe cases.
ST_VisionArchives.Boombox_VisionDescAfter:
This Object Anomaly consists of a set of electronic music production and performance equipment decorated with graffiti, including CD controllers, displays, and sound systems. These devices can operate without power and combine into a creature-like form that moves autonomously, active in the Clement Music Corner.
The Beat King appears as abandoned equipment scattered across the plaza when dormant. When activated, it hovers and begins its performance, challenging people in the plaza to the "Boss Track Challenge."
During the "Boss Track Challenge," the Beat King plays its original electronic music and creates glowing projections that indicate volume levels. It attacks challengers following rhythms that match the music's beat, forming pixel graphics similar to 8-bit games that prompt challengers to make actions matching the beat. If challengers don't cooperate with its performance or if they make mistakes, the Anomaly becomes upset and unleashes merciless sound wave attacks.
Additionally, multiple verifications confirm that the Beat King's music has no negative effects on humans. The production quality is excellent with a unique style that shares similarities with the early works of a certain famous electronic musician.
ST_VisionArchives.PObⅠS-7605_VisionDescBefore:
This Object Anomaly resembles an old-fashioned projector. It tends to create fabricated videos at the sites of its appearance, mostly footage involving incidents. Participants can explore further at any point during the video's progress. Once the nexus in the video is found—usually the source of the incident—the Spacetime Projector will naturally undergo nullification.
Interestingly, each time the Spacetime Projector is nullified, it plays a message. Out of the 47 messages officially recorded, 7 mention something about aiding the spacetime they are in. Based on the content of each message, some experts believe that the content displayed by the Spacetime Projector involves incidents that occurred in other timelines, and the incidents themselves become negated through the nullification of the Spacetime Projector. However, some experts also consider this to be merely a farce orchestrated by the Spacetime Projector itself.

ST_VisionArchives.Anomaly0094_RecordBeforeContent_2:
What comes to mind when you think of school? Endless homework? Sweat pouring down on the playground? Or the irrepressible anticipation for summer vacation, even during exams? Eventually, we all leave school and graduate. With the final bell, our student days end before we realize it.
Many of us dream of those irretrievable youthful days. Today, Mr. Noel shares with us his experience of literally stepping back into that "unreturnable" school building.
"Hello, Chatty. I'm your loyal listener. Hearing you narrate those magical stories is one of my most cherished memories of youth." Thank you! Thank you for your support! Chatty is honored to have been with you all this time.
"Like many others, I went to college, graduated, and started working. I followed the path everyone takes, accepting an ordinary, normal life. The shining experiences of my youth seemed to have faded and withered with time. I thought… they were gone for good. But then, it happened. A grand adventure I never thought possible for someone as ordinary as me."
"That day was terrible. It was nearly dawn when I left work. The weather was awful too, and I was soaked without an umbrella. As if I needed more trouble, I encountered that anomaly. The street's vending machines were lifted, arranged, and combined by an invisible hand, forming a solid wall. This should have been a sight I'd dreamed of as a child, but at that moment, it was just an exhausting, frustrating obstacle blocking my way home."
"I just wanted to get home, collapse into bed, and catch a breath from endless work. Why was even this simple wish obstructed? I turned around angrily, trying to find a route home that would shelter me from the rain without too much of a detour. The gears in my brain felt rusted by the rain, creaking before falling apart, scattering useless mental scrap everywhere. Even something this simple was beyond me in my exhausted state."
"Maybe it was a sudden gust making my drenched body shiver, or seeing the cold, imposing lights of the office building where people were still working overtime, or perhaps I simply couldn't think of anything to do in this situation. Whatever it was, call it divine intervention or giving up, my body drove me towards that red door. I knew very well I wasn't looking for shelter from the rain."
"Inside wasn't a volcanic eruption or a raging tsunami, nor a fairytale gingerbread house or cotton candy forest. It was just an abandoned, overgrown building site. Utterly ordinary. Only a vibrant door in the distance, starkly contrasting with the gloomy surroundings, reminded me where I was. From the other side of the door wafted the faint smell of paper, ink, and raw wood. Familiar, pleasant scents that felt safe, like something I'd known long, long ago."
"The library. The library in my old school building."
"When was the last time I'd properly read a book in a library? A box of memories seemed to spring open in my mind. School days, manga magazines in the school library, movie specials, the latest Anomalies Guide… Back then, I was reluctant to go to school, often skipping classes I didn't like to spend whole days mushrooming in the library. Daydreaming based on the adventures in books, fantasizing about experiencing such wonderful anomaly stories myself!"
"And indeed, an adventure did happen to me. The school building mysteriously "disappeared" on the first day of a new semester. Teachers stared at each other in bewilderment at the large pit where the building used to be, forced to postpone the start of school. The gloomy-faced students instantly brightened up and scattered. No school was amazing! It must have been fate!"
"But back then, we were just secretly happy about no classes, no homework, no exams. We never thought about what our student life really meant."
"And now, that school building I thought I'd never see again was right before my eyes."
"Seeing it again, I realized how much I wanted to come back here, how much I wanted to go back to school."
"I still knew the classrooms so well, surely there was still a failed test paper folded into a paper airplane in the desk drawer. I shouted and jumped around like a madman, desperate to throw myself onto that small desk and chair. At that moment, I felt like I was back in my youth, full of boundless energy. I started running down the hallway, feeling as light and free as in the past. But soon I had to lean against the wall, gasping for breath, my knees making an all-too-appropriate cracking sound."
"By this time, I had reached the end of the school building. That door, so vividly red as if the paint had just been applied, appeared before me again. It was open, with a steady curtain of rain beyond it."
"If I went out, everything would end. I'd be drenched by the rain of reality again, and if I told others about this experience, they'd just look at me suspiciously, saying it must be delirious ramblings from a cold."
"This place was my sanctuary. It safeguarded the time I had lost, and that's why we met again—I firmly believed this. I wanted to stay. I had to stay."
"I put my hand on the doorknob, firmly pulling it closed."
"The door shut. And then… as if telling me I couldn't stay, that I couldn't go back, this space gradually dissolved and disappeared completely. I was back in the pouring rain, no different from before I entered that door."
"So that's how it is."
"The door, the wall, they all vanished. Everything that could prove I had returned to that school building was gone. It all happened so fast—was it just a dream born from my exhaustion? Or was my body temperature so abnormal that I needed urgent medical care?"
"Perhaps none of that matters. I only need to know that those lost times are still treasured somewhere, and that's enough."
"Maybe… the chance to meet again is already the most dazzling miracle. For me, this was the greatest adventure I could have hoped to encounter."

…This is where the letter ends. Thank you for sharing, Mr. Noel. Chatty is honored to have received your letter and witnessed this adventure with you and countless listeners. Lastly, Chatty wants to say: We may encounter many disappointments and sadness, making life feel dull and gray. But no matter what, please do not give up hope and dreams. They may come to you at any moment, waiting for you to witness them. In fact, they might be happening quietly, as long as you are willing to believe.
ST_VisionArchives.Boombox_RecordBefore_2:
Huh? An interview now? I'm gonna be late clocking in… But answering citizens' questions is part of the job too… O-okay, let's make it quick then!
The Beat King… Oh! That super loud Anomaly! I definitely fought it before!
That day I was on duty near Illusion Town when suddenly a student ran up to me, saying there was an Anomaly attacking citizens on the east side of Clement Academy! I thought saving people was the priority, so I rushed right over. From way off I could hear this… really trendy, upbeat music? When I got to the scene, there were several unconscious students lying scattered on the ground! That Anomaly, which looked like a pile of speakers and keyboards cobbled together, spotted me and sent this massive sound wave charging at me…
It was such a headache! I didn't know this Anomaly's behavior patterns, and I wasn't sure about the students' injuries. In desperation, I could only rely on my reflexes to dodge its attacks while avoiding making it angry enough to hurt the students… I slowly realized its moves had this fixed "boom-boom-pow" rhythm! After successfully dodging several rounds of attacks, I figured out its pattern. I started moving to the beat while carrying the students out of its activity range.
Luckily it didn't chase after us, just went back to the center of the area and played music all alone. Before long it quieted down and turned back into a pile of ordinary equipment. Speaking of which, that thing had this really complex smell… like dust and rust, but also like something burnt, the kind that makes you want to wrinkle your nose!

Since saving people was urgent, my colleague and I rushed them to the hospital. Thankfully everyone was fine… I heard from them that there was a trending challenge on Bagel, competing to see who could dodge the Beat King's attacks the most times in a row, and they'd record videos to post on Bagel! So much trouble… Oh right! There was also some bystander who recorded me rescuing people and posted it online, even though that's not allowed!
And that video got super high views! The comments were all saying stuff I couldn't understand, like "frame-perfect timing," "combo master," "perfect clear"… I have no idea what any of that means!

Recently, we have noticed discussions on Bagel comparing the classic design of DeLuxur Home's older robot vacuum models with the appearance of the Anomaly known as the Rain-sweeping Maid. We sincerely thank everyone for their keen observations and enthusiastic associations, and we are pleased to officially respond: Yes, DeLuxur Home's robot vacuums do bear a striking resemblance to the Rain-sweeping Maid.
However, we must solemnly clarify a long-standing misconception: DeLuxur Home's robot vacuums do not employ the trendy "Anomalize" design philosophy that is popular today. In fact, quite the opposite is true. It is the Rain-sweeping Maid, an Anomaly that shares our commitment to cleanliness and lofty ideals, that has been influenced by the trends we pioneered.
DeLuxur Home was among the first home appliance companies to introduce robot vacuums to Hethereau. We are delighted to see that, years later, our robot vacuums and floor cleaners have become indispensable cleaning companions in countless households. Providing quality products at affordable prices and creating convenience for our citizens' lives has been our brand's mission since its founding. Our first-generation robot vacuum featured a rounded body, flexible hose, and easy-to-clean suction port, the result of a perfect union between function and aesthetics.
According to the Hethereau Anomaly Yearbook, the Rain-sweeping Maid's appearance began to change approximately one year after our products hit the market. Sales data from that year shows that over half of all households in Hethereau purchased our products. DeLuxur Home can proudly proclaim that the striking similarity between today's Rain-sweeping Maid and our products represents not only their own evolution toward greater efficiency and beauty, but also proof of the market's overwhelming approval of our designs.
We are also honored to take this opportunity to announce that DeLuxur Home's next-generation robot vacuum will be officially unveiled soon.
We do more than just clear away rainwater. We make every corner of your home shine like new.
We cannot dispel the clouds, but we can still bring you a sunny disposition.
We believe that in the next generation, the Rain-sweeping Maid will continue to evolve alongside us. DeLuxur Home: Always Defining Lifestyle Trends.

ST_VisionArchives.Boss08_Record_3:
After all these years, people are still asking about that urban legend?
Yes, Butterfly was my classmate. She was quiet, got good grades, and had a happy family. A well-behaved kid from an ordinary household. If there were a template for an average life, her first dozen years would have been exactly that.
One day, she started skipping class. At first, no one thought she would ever skip. Everyone assumed she was sick and just forgot to call in. The teacher thought so too, until they finally reached her parents on the third day and found out she wasn't sick at all. They went to the cinema in New Herland and dragged her back. Two days later, she skipped again, so her parents took her home and made her reflect on her actions. Everyone thought she'd come back eventually. They kept setting aside test papers for her, until her drawer, her desk, and her chair were all piled high. Only then did it dawn on everyone that she probably wasn't coming back.
Of course there were dark assumptions, but without any news or evidence, we couldn't be sure what actually happened. The teacher said she was skipping class to watch movies. Her backpack was stuffed with ticket stubs. The first time I saw Swallowtail, its skeletal frame rustling in the wind… It reminded me of when the teacher picked up Little Butterfly's backpack, and the ticket stubs rustling out just the same.
On graduation day, I wanted to sort through Little Butterfly's things. Her books, test papers, and ticket stubs. At least keep them safe for her. But when I got there, everything was gone. I checked the security footage. Someone I didn't recognize had taken it all to sell as scrap. Probably didn't get more than a few Fons. Not even enough for half a movie ticket.
Sorry, I got off track. Anything else you want to ask?
"Sky"? Let me think… There was no one by that name in our class. No one with that character in their name either. Yeah, I'm sure.
ST_VisionArchives.Lamp_RecordBefore_1:
We've been having constant blackouts around here lately. Every night it's pitch black and you can't see a thing.
At first everyone said it was just routine maintenance, and figured it'd be fixed the next day. The next day was the same though, so we thought it'd have be fixed by the third day. Well, many days have passed now and we still have no power at night, that's when people started to think something was off.
I heard from others that it's some sneaky "Power Saver" causing trouble. The guy can't stand how our area is all bright and lively every day, thinks it's a waste of electricity, so every night he goes and cuts the power to this whole block. But that doesn't make much sense, right? The money he saves on electricity bills doesn't go into his pocket anyway, so what's the point?
You're asking why I don't seem worried about this at all?
…Guess how late I have to work overtime at the company every night? Whether there's power at home or not makes absolutely no difference to me…
ST_VisionArchives.Boss08_Record_2:
This Anomaly was quite beautiful. The backyard was a bit empty, so I thought I'd bring it back to Eibon. I tried to contain it using some old equipment I brought from the Bureau, but the moment it was contained, it turned into a thin sheet of paper. Not pretty at all! I shrugged, then decided to let it out and set it free.
This butterfly, it isn't as dangerous as they say. Small animals use camouflage to blend into their environment and protect themselves, but it couldn't care less about that. It painted itself in vivid colors. For the sake of that beauty, it has to face even more danger. Acting aggressive is just another way it protects itself. Don't we already know this? It won't attack first, it's gentle.
Nullification… With the way it presents itself, nullification is only a matter of time. After all, the objective danger it poses can't be denied. This was also its own choice. It's just a shame about those beautiful wings…
ST_VisionArchives.Mammon_RecordBefore_1: This cat is pretty famous in our pet lover group. At first, we all thought it must have an owner since stray cats are rarely this clean, not to mention all those shiny accessories it wears. One of our group members works in jewelry, and he said any single gem from that collection could buy you a large open flat in central Miguel District. Here's the weird part: lots of us have seen it while feeding strays. It has a pretty good temperament, won't let you pet it but doesn't bite either. Someone in the group tried to adopt it, but after finishing the Froze'n'Dried treats, it just ran off. Couldn't even catch a single whisker. Whenever I've encountered it, it's been pretty bossy. It always eats up all the fish snacks I bring, then rubs against me demanding more. Maybe it became a stray because it just eats too much?
